texts.mrk.11.7: E levaram o jumentinho a Jesus, e lançaram sobre elle os seus vestidos, e assentou-se sobre elle:
texts.mrk.11.8: E muitos estendiam os seus vestidos pelo caminho, e outros cortavam ramos das arvores, e os espalhavam pelo caminho.
texts.mrk.11.9: E aquelles que iam adiante, e os que seguiam, clamavam, dizendo: Hosanna, bemdito o que vem em nome do Senhor;
texts.mrk.11.10: Bemdito o reino do nosso pae David, que vem em nome do Senhor; Hosanna nas alturas.
texts.mrk.11.11: E Jesus entrou em Jerusalem, no templo, e, tendo visto tudo em redor, e sendo já tarde, saiu para Bethania com os doze.
texts.mrk.11.12: E, no dia seguinte, quando sairam de Bethania, teve fome,
texts.mrk.11.13: E, vendo de longe uma figueira que tinha folhas, foi vêr se n’ella acharia alguma coisa: e, chegando a ella, não achou senão folhas, porque não era tempo de figos.
texts.mrk.11.14: E Jesus, fallando, disse á figueira: Nunca mais alguem coma fructo de ti, para sempre. E os seus discípulos ouviram isto.
texts.mrk.11.15: E vieram a Jerusalem; e Jesus, entrando no templo, começou a expulsar os que vendiam e compravam no templo; e derribou as mesas dos cambiadores e as cadeiras dos que vendiam pombas.
texts.mrk.11.16: E não consentia que alguem levasse algum vaso pelo templo.
texts.mrk.11.17: E os ensinava, dizendo: Não está escripto: A minha casa será chamada por todas as nações casa de oração? Mas vós a tendes feito covil de ladrões.
texts.mrk.11.18: E os escribas e principes dos sacerdotes, tendo ouvido isto, buscavam occasião para o matar; pois elles o temiam, porque toda a multidão estava admirada ácerca da sua doutrina.
texts.mrk.11.19: E, sendo já tarde, saiu fóra da cidade.
texts.mrk.11.20: E elles, passando pela manhã, viram que a figueira se tinha seccado desde as raizes.
texts.mrk.11.21: E Pedro, lembrando-se, disse-lhe: Mestre, eis que a figueira, que tu amaldiçoaste, seccou-se.
texts.mrk.11.22: E Jesus, respondendo, disse-lhes: Tende fé em Deus;
texts.mrk.11.23: Porque em verdade vos digo que qualquer que disser a este monte: Ergue-te e lança-te no mar; e não duvidar em seu coração, mas crêr que se fará aquillo que diz, tudo o que disser lhe será feito.
texts.mrk.11.24: Portanto vos digo que tudo o que pedirdes, orando, crêde que o recebereis, e tel-o-heis;
texts.mrk.11.25: E, quando estiverdes orando, perdoae, se tendes alguma coisa contra alguém, para que vosso Pae, que está nos céus, vos perdôe as vossas offensas;
texts.mrk.11.26: Mas, se vós não perdoardes, tambem vosso Pae, que está nos céus, vos não perdoará as vossas offensas.
texts.mrk.11.27: E tornaram a Jerusalem, e, andando elle pelo templo, os principaes dos sacerdotes, e os escribas, e os anciãos se approximaram d’elle,
texts.mrk.11.28: E lhe disseram: Com que auctoridade fazes tu estas coisas? e quem te deu esta auctoridade para fazer estas coisas?
texts.mrk.11.29: Más Jesus, respondendo, disse-lhes: Também eu vos perguntarei uma coisa, e respondei-me, e vos direi com que auctoridade faço estas coisas:
texts.mrk.11.30: O baptismo de João era do céu ou dos homens? respondei-me.
texts.mrk.11.31: E elles arrazoavam entre si, dizendo: Se dissermos: Do céu; elle nos dirá: Pois porque o não crêstes?
texts.mrk.11.32: Se, porém, dissermos: Dos homens; tememos o povo. Porque todos sustentavam que João verdadeiramente era propheta.
texts.mrk.11.33: E, respondendo, disseram a Jesus: Não sabemos. E Jesus, respondendo, lhes disse: Tambem eu vos não direi com que auctoridade faço estas coisas.
texts.mrk.12.1: E começou a fallar-lhes por parabolas: Um homem plantou uma vinha, e cercou-a de um vallado, e fundou n’ella um lagar, e edificou uma torre, e arrendou-a a uns lavradores, e partiu para fóra da terra;
texts.mrk.12.2: E, chegado o tempo, mandou um servo aos lavradores para que recebesse, dos lavradores, do fructo da vinha.
texts.mrk.12.3: Mas elles, apoderando-se d’elle, o feriram e o mandaram embora vasio.
texts.mrk.12.4: E tornou a enviar-lhes outro servo; e elles, apedrejando-o, o feriram na cabeça, e o mandaram embora, tendo-o affrontado.
texts.mrk.12.5: E tornou a enviar-lhes outro, e a este mataram, e outros muitos, e feriram uns, e mataram outros.
texts.mrk.12.6: Tendo elle pois ainda um seu filho amado, enviou-o tambem a estes por derradeiro, dizendo: Ao menos terão respeito ao meu filho.
texts.mrk.12.7: Mas aquelles lavradores disseram entre si: Este é o herdeiro; vamos, matemol-o, e a herança será nossa.
texts.mrk.12.8: E, pegando d’elle, o mataram, e o lançaram fóra da vinha.
texts.mrk.12.9: Que fará pois o Senhor da vinha? Virá, e destruirá os lavradores, e dará a vinha a outros.
texts.mrk.12.10: Ainda não lestes esta Escriptura: A pedra, que os edificadores rejeitaram, esta foi posta por cabeça da esquina:
texts.mrk.12.11: Isto foi feito pelo Senhor, e é coisa maravilhosa aos nossos olhos?
texts.mrk.12.12: E buscavam prendel-o, mas temiam a multidão, porque entendiam que contra elles dizia esta parabola: e, deixando-o, foram-se.
texts.mrk.12.13: E enviaram-lhe alguns dos phariseos e dos herodianos, para que o apanhassem n’alguma palavra.
texts.mrk.12.14: E, chegando elles, disseram-lhe: Mestre, sabemos que és homem de verdade, e de ninguem se te dá, porque não olhas á apparencia dos homens, antes com verdade ensinas o caminho de Deus: é licito dar o tributo a Cesar, ou não? Daremos, ou não daremos?
texts.mrk.12.15: Então ele, conhecendo a sua hypocrisia, disse-lhes: Porque me tentaes? trazei-me uma moeda, para que a veja.
texts.mrk.12.16: E elles lh’a trouxeram. E disse-lhes: De quem é esta imagem e inscripção? E elles lhe disseram: De Cesar.
texts.mrk.12.17: E Jesus, respondendo, disse-lhes: Dae pois a Cesar o que é de Cesar, e a Deus o que é de Deus. E maravilharam-se d’elle.
texts.mrk.12.18: Então os sadduceos, que dizem que não ha resurreição, approximaram-se d’elle, e perguntaram-lhe, dizendo:
texts.mrk.12.19: Mestre, Moysés nos escreveu que, se morresse o irmão de alguem, e deixasse mulher e não deixasse filhos, seu irmão tomasse a mulher d’elle, e suscitasse semente a seu irmão.
texts.mrk.12.20: Ora havia sete irmãos, e o primeiro tomou mulher, e morreu sem deixar semente;
texts.mrk.12.21: E o segundo tambem a tomou e morreu, e nem este deixou semente; e o terceiro da mesma maneira;
texts.mrk.12.22: E tomaram-n’a todos os sete, sem, comtudo, deixarem semente. Finalmente, depois de todos, morreu tambem a mulher.
texts.mrk.12.23: Na resurreição, pois, quando resuscitarem, de qual d’estes será a mulher? porque os sete a tiveram por mulher.
texts.mrk.12.24: E Jesus, respondendo, disse-lhes: Porventura não erraes vós, porque não sabeis as Escripturas nem o poder de Deus?
texts.mrk.12.25: Porquanto, quando resuscitarem dos mortos, nem casarão, nem se darão em casamento, mas serão como os anjos que estão nos céus.
texts.mrk.12.26: E, ácerca dos mortos que houverem de resuscitar, não tendes lido no livro de Moysés como Deus lhe fallou na sarça, dizendo: Eu sou o Deus de Abrahão, e o Deus de Isaac, e o Deus de Jacob?
texts.mrk.12.27: Ora Deus não é dos mortos, mas sim Deus dos vivos. Por isso vós erraes muito.
texts.mrk.12.28: E, approximando-se d’elle um dos escribas que os tinha ouvido disputar, sabendo que lhes tinha respondido bem, perguntou-lhe: Qual é o primeiro de todos os mandamentos?
texts.mrk.12.29: E Jesus respondeu-lhe: O primeiro de todos os mandamentos é: Ouve, Israel, o Senhor nosso Deus é o unico Senhor.
texts.mrk.12.30: Amarás, pois, o Senhor teu Deus de todo o teu coração, e de toda a tua alma, e de todo o teu entendimento, e de todas as tuas forças: este é o primeiro mandamento.
texts.mrk.12.31: E o segundo, similhante a este, é: Amarás o teu proximo como a ti mesmo. Não ha outro mandamento maior do que estes.
texts.mrk.12.32: E o escriba lhe disse: Muito bem, Mestre, e com verdade disseste que ha um só Deus, e que não ha outro além d’elle;
texts.mrk.12.33: E que amal-o de todo o coração, e de todo o entendimento, e de toda a alma, e de todas as forças, e amar o proximo como a si mesmo, é mais do que todos os holocaustos e sacrificios.
texts.mrk.12.34: E Jesus, vendo que havia respondido sabiamente, disse-lhe: Não estás longe do reino de Deus. E já ninguem ousava perguntar-lhe mais nada.
texts.mrk.12.35: E, fallando Jesus, dizia, ensinando no templo: Como dizem os escribas que o Christo é filho de David?
texts.mrk.12.36: Porque o mesmo David disse pelo Espirito Sancto: O Senhor disse ao meu Senhor: Assenta-te á minha direita até que eu ponha os teus inimigos por escabello dos teus pés.
texts.mrk.12.37: Pois, se David mesmo lhe chama Senhor, como é logo seu filho? E a grande multidão o ouvia de boa vontade.
texts.mrk.12.38: E, ensinando-os, dizia-lhes: Guardae-vos dos escribas, que gostam de andar com vestidos compridos, e das saudações nas praças,
texts.mrk.12.39: E das primeiras cadeiras nas synagogas, e dos primeiros assentos nas ceias;
texts.mrk.12.40: Que devoram as casas das viuvas, e isso com pretexto de largas orações. Estes receberão mais grave condemnação.
texts.mrk.12.41: E, estando Jesus assentado defronte da arca do thesouro, observava a maneira como a multidão lançava o dinheiro na arca do thesouro; e muitos ricos deitavam muito.
texts.mrk.12.42: E, chegando uma pobre viuva, deitou duas pequenas moedas, que valiam quatro réis.
texts.mrk.12.43: E, chamando os seus discipulos, disse-lhes: Em verdade vos digo que esta pobre viuva deitou mais do que todos os que deitaram na arca do thesouro,
texts.mrk.12.44: Porque todos ali deitaram do que lhes sobejava, mas esta, da sua pobreza, deitou tudo o que tinha, todo o seu sustento.
texts.mrk.13.1: E, saindo elle do templo, disse-lhe um dos seus discipulos: Mestre, olha que pedras, e que edificios!
texts.mrk.13.2: E, respondendo Jesus, disse-lhe: Vês estes grandes edificios? Não ficará pedra sobre pedra que não seja derribada.
texts.mrk.13.3: E, assentando-se elle no monte das Oliveiras, defronte do templo, Pedro, e Thiago, e João e André lhe perguntaram em particular:
texts.mrk.13.4: Dize-nos, quando serão essas coisas, e que signal haverá quando todas essas coisas se houverem de cumprir.
texts.mrk.13.5: E Jesus, respondendo-lhes, começou a dizer: Olhae que ninguem vos engane;
texts.mrk.13.6: Porque muitos virão em meu nome, dizendo: Eu sou o Christo: e enganarão a muitos.
texts.mrk.13.7: E, quando ouvirdes de guerras e de rumores de guerras, não vos turbeis; porque assim importa fazer-se; mas ainda não será o fim.
texts.mrk.13.8: Porque se levantará nação contra nação, e reino contra reino, e haverá terremotos em diversos logares, e haverá fomes e alvoroços. Estas coisas serão o principio de dôres.
texts.mrk.13.9: Mas olhae por vós mesmos, porque vos entregarão aos concilios e ás synagogas; sereis açoitados, e sereis apresentados ante presidentes e reis, por amor de mim, para lhes servir de testemunho.
texts.mrk.13.10: Mas importa que o evangelho se pregue primeiro entre todas as gentes.
texts.mrk.13.11: Quando pois vos conduzirem para vos entregarem, não estejaes solicitos d’antemão pelo que haveis de dizer; mas, o que vos fôr dado n’aquella hora, isso fallae; porque não sois vós os que fallaes, mas o Espirito Sancto.
texts.mrk.13.12: E o irmão entregará á morte o irmão, e o pae o filho: e levantar-se-hão os filhos contra os paes, e os matarão.
texts.mrk.13.13: E sereis aborrecidos por todos por amor do meu nome; mas quem perseverar até ao fim esse será salvo.
texts.mrk.13.14: Ora, quando vós virdes a abominação do assolamento, que foi predito, estando onde não deve estar (quem lê, entenda), então os que estiverem na Judea fujam para os montes.
texts.mrk.13.15: E o que estiver sobre o telhado não desça para casa, nem entre a tomar coisa alguma de sua casa;
texts.mrk.13.16: E o que estiver no campo não volte atraz, para tomar o seu vestido.
texts.mrk.13.17: Mas ai das gravidas, e das que criarem n’aquelles dias!
texts.mrk.13.18: Orae pois, para que a vossa fugida não succeda no inverno;
texts.mrk.13.19: Porque n’aquelles dias haverá uma afflicção tal, qual nunca houve desde o principio da creação, que Deus creou, até agora, nem tão pouco haverá.
texts.mrk.13.20: E, se o Senhor não abreviasse aquelles dias, nenhuma carne se salvaria; mas, por causa dos escolhidos que escolheu, abreviou aquelles dias.
texts.mrk.13.21: E então, se alguem vos disser: Eis aqui está o Christo: ou, Eil-o ali está: não o acrediteis.
texts.mrk.13.22: Porque se levantarão falsos christos, e falsos prophetas, e farão signaes e prodigios, para enganarem, se fôr possivel, até os escolhidos.
texts.mrk.13.23: Mas vós vede; eis que d’antemão vos tenho dito tudo.
texts.mrk.13.24: Ora, n’aquelles dias, depois d’aquella afflicção, o sol se escurecerá, e a lua não dará o seu resplendor,
texts.mrk.13.25: E as estrellas cairão do céu, e as forças que estão nos céus serão abaladas.
texts.mrk.13.26: E então verão vir o Filho do homem nas nuvens, com grande poder e gloria.
texts.mrk.13.27: E então enviará os seus anjos, e ajuntará os seus escolhidos, desde os quatro ventos, da extremidade da terra até á extremidade do céu.
texts.mrk.13.28: Aprendei pois a parabola da figueira: Quando já o seu ramo se torna tenro, e brota folhas, bem sabeis que já está proximo o verão.
texts.mrk.13.29: Assim tambem vós, quando virdes succederem estas coisas, sabei que já está junto ás portas.
texts.mrk.13.30: Na verdade vos digo que não passará esta geração, até que todas estas coisas aconteçam.
texts.mrk.13.31: Passará o céu e a terra, mas as minhas palavras não passarão.
texts.mrk.13.32: Porém d’aquelle dia e hora ninguem sabe, nem os anjos que estão no céu, nem o Filho, senão o Pae.
texts.mrk.13.33: Olhae, vigiae e orae; porque não sabeis quando chegará o tempo.
texts.mrk.13.34: Como o homem, que, partindo para fóra da terra, deixou a sua casa, e deu auctoridade aos seus servos, e a cada um a sua obra, e mandou ao porteiro que vigiasse;
texts.mrk.13.35: Vigiae pois, porque não sabeis quando virá o senhor da casa; se á tarde, se á meia noite, se ao cantar do gallo, se pela manhã,
texts.mrk.13.36: Para que não venha de improviso, e vos ache dormindo.
texts.mrk.13.37: E as coisas que vos digo digo-as a todos: Vigiae.
texts.mrk.14.1: E d’alli a dois dias era a paschoa, e a festa dos pães asmos, e os principaes dos sacerdotes e os escribas buscavam como o prenderiam com dolo, e o matariam.
texts.mrk.14.2: Mas elles diziam: Não na festa, para que porventura se não faça alvoroço entre o povo.
texts.mrk.14.3: E, estando elle em Bethania, assentado á mesa, em casa de Simão, o leproso, veiu uma mulher, que trazia um vaso de alabastro, com unguento de nardo puro, de muito preço, e, quebrando o vaso, lh’o derramou sobre a cabeça.
texts.mrk.14.4: E alguns houve que em si mesmos se indignaram, e disseram: Para que se fez este desperdicio de unguento?
texts.mrk.14.5: Porque podia isto vender-se por mais de trezentos dinheiros, e dal-o aos pobres. E bramavam contra ella.
texts.mrk.14.6: Jesus, porém, disse: Deixae-a, para que a molestaes? Ella fez-me uma obra boa.
texts.mrk.14.7: Porque sempre tendes os pobres comvosco, e podeis fazer-lhes bem, quando quizerdes; porém a mim nem sempre me tendes.
texts.mrk.14.8: Esta fez o que podia; antecipou-se a ungir o meu corpo para a sepultura.
texts.mrk.14.9: Em verdade vos digo que, em todas as partes do mundo onde este evangelho fôr prégado, tambem o que ella fez será contado para sua memoria.
texts.mrk.14.10: E Judas Iscariotes, um dos doze, foi ter com os principaes dos sacerdotes para lh’o entregar.
texts.mrk.14.11: E elles, ouvindo-o, folgaram, e prometteram dar-lhe dinheiro; e buscava como o entregaria a tempo opportuno.
texts.mrk.14.12: E, no primeiro dia dos pães asmos, quando sacrificavam a paschoa, disseram-lhe os discipulos: Aonde queres que vamos preparar-te o necessario para comer a paschoa?
texts.mrk.14.13: E enviou dois dos seus discipulos, e disse-lhes: Ide á cidade, e um homem, que leva um cantaro d’agua, vos encontrará; segui-o;
texts.mrk.14.14: E, onde quer que entrar, dizei ao senhor da casa: O Mestre diz: Onde está o aposento em que hei de comer a paschoa com os meus discipulos?
texts.mrk.14.15: E elle vos mostrará um grande cenaculo mobilado e preparado; ali a preparae.
texts.mrk.14.16: E, saindo os seus discipulos, foram á cidade, e acharam como lhes tinha dito, e prepararam a paschoa.
texts.mrk.14.17: E, chegada a tarde, foi com os doze,
texts.mrk.14.18: E, quando estavam assentados á mesa, e comendo, disse Jesus: Em verdade vos digo que um de vos, que comigo come, ha de trahir-me.
texts.mrk.14.19: E elles começaram a entristecer-se e a dizer-lhe um após outro: Porventura sou eu, Senhor? e outro: Porventura sou eu, Senhor?
texts.mrk.14.20: Porém elle, respondendo, disse-lhes: É um dos doze que mette comigo a mão no prato.
texts.mrk.14.21: Na verdade o Filho do homem vae, como d’elle está escripto, mas ai d’aquelle homem por quem o Filho do homem é trahido! bom seria ao tal homem não haver nascido.
texts.mrk.14.22: E, comendo elles, tomou Jesus pão, e, abençoando-o, o partiu e deu-lh’o, e disse: Tomae, comei, isto é o meu corpo.
texts.mrk.14.23: E, tomando o calix, e dando graças, deu-lh’o; e todos beberam d’elle.
texts.mrk.14.24: E disse-lhes: Isto é o meu sangue, o sangue do Novo Testamento, que por muitos é derramado.
texts.mrk.14.25: Em verdade vos digo que não beberei mais do fructo da vide, até áquelle dia em que o beber novo no reino de Deus.
texts.mrk.14.26: E, tendo cantado o hymno, sairam para o monte das Oliveiras.
texts.mrk.14.27: E disse-lhes Jesus: Todos vós esta noite vos escandalizareis em mim; porque escripto está: Ferirei o pastor, e as ovelhas se dispersarão.
texts.mrk.14.28: Mas, depois que eu houver resuscitado, irei adiante de vós para a Galilea.
texts.mrk.14.29: E disse-lhe Pedro: Ainda que todos se escandalizem, nunca, porém, eu.
texts.mrk.14.30: E disse-lhe Jesus: Em verdade te digo que hoje, n’esta noite, antes que o gallo cante duas vezes, tres vezes me negarás.
texts.mrk.14.31: Mas elle dizia cada vez mais: Ainda que me seja necessario morrer comtigo, de modo nenhum te negarei. E da mesma maneira diziam todos tambem.
texts.mrk.14.32: E foram a um logar chamado Gethsemane, e disse aos seus discipulos: Assentae-vos aqui, até que ore.
texts.mrk.14.33: E tomou comsigo a Pedro, e a Thiago, e a João, e começou a ter pavor, e a angustiar-se.
texts.mrk.14.34: E disse-lhes: A minha alma está profundamente triste até á morte: ficae aqui, e vigiae.
texts.mrk.14.35: E, tendo ido um pouco mais adiante, prostrou-se em terra; e orou para que, se fosse possivel, passasse d’elle aquella hora.
texts.mrk.14.36: E disse: Abba, Pae, todas as coisas te são possiveis; affasta de mim este calix; porém não o que eu quero, mas o que tu queres.
texts.mrk.14.37: E, chegando, achou-os dormindo; e disse a Pedro: Simão, dormes? não podes vigiar uma hora?
texts.mrk.14.38: Vigiae e orae, para que não entreis em tentação; o espirito, na verdade, está prompto, mas a carne é fraca.
texts.mrk.14.39: E, tornando a ir, orou, dizendo as mesmas palavras.
texts.mrk.14.40: E, tornando, achou-os outra vez dormindo, porque os seus olhos estavam carregados, e não sabiam que responder-lhe.
texts.mrk.14.41: E voltou terceira vez, e disse-lhes: Dormi agora, e descançae. Basta; é chegada a hora. Eis que o Filho do homem vae ser entregue nas mãos dos peccadores.
texts.mrk.14.42: Levantae-vos, vamos; eis que está perto o que me trahe.
texts.mrk.14.43: E logo, fallando elle ainda, veiu Judas, que era um dos doze, da parte dos principaes dos sacerdotes, e dos escribas e dos anciãos, e com elle uma grande multidão com espadas e varapaus.
texts.mrk.14.44: Ora, o que o trahia, tinha-lhes dado um signal, dizendo: Aquelle que eu beijar, esse é; prendei-o, e levae-o com segurança.
texts.mrk.14.45: E, logo que chegou, approximou-se d’elle, e disse-lhe: Rabbi, Rabbi. E beijou-o.
texts.mrk.14.46: E lançaram-lhe as mãos, e o prenderam.
texts.mrk.14.47: E um dos que ali estavam presentes, puxando da espada, feriu o servo do summo sacerdote, e cortou-lhe a orelha.
texts.mrk.14.48: E, respondendo Jesus, disse-lhes: Saistes com espadas e varapaus a prender-me, como a um salteador?
texts.mrk.14.49: Todos os dias estava comvosco ensinando no templo, e não me prendestes; mas assim se faz para que as Escripturas se cumpram.
texts.mrk.14.51: E um certo mancebo o seguia, envolto em um lençol sobre o corpo nú. E os mancebos o prenderam;
texts.mrk.14.52: E elle, largando o lençol, fugiu nú d’entre elles.
texts.mrk.14.53: E levaram Jesus ao summo sacerdote, e ajuntaram-se a elle todos os principaes dos sacerdotes, e os anciãos e os escribas.
texts.mrk.14.54: E Pedro o seguiu de longe até dentro do pateo do summo sacerdote, e estava assentado com os servidores, e aquentando-se ao lume.
texts.mrk.14.55: E os principaes dos sacerdotes e todo o concilio buscavam algum testemunho contra Jesus, para o matar, e não o achavam.
texts.mrk.14.56: Porque muitos testificavam falsamente contra elle, mas os testemunhos não eram conformes.
texts.mrk.14.57: E, levantando-se alguns, testificavam falsamente contra elle, dizendo:
texts.mrk.14.58: Nós ouvimos-lhe dizer: Eu derribarei este templo, construido pelas mãos, e em tres dias edificarei outro, não feito por mãos.
texts.mrk.14.59: E nem assim o seu testemunho era conforme.
texts.mrk.14.60: E, levantando-se o summo sacerdote no meio, perguntou a Jesus, dizendo: Nada respondes? Que testificam estes contra ti?
texts.mrk.14.61: Mas elle calou-se, e nada respondeu. O summo sacerdote lhe tornou a perguntar, e disse-lhe: És tu o Christo, Filho do Deus Bemdito?
texts.mrk.14.62: E Jesus disse-lhe: Eu o sou, e vereis o Filho do homem assentado á direita do poder de Deus, e vindo sobre as nuvens do céu.
texts.mrk.14.63: E o summo sacerdote, rasgando os seus vestidos, disse: Para que necessitamos de mais testemunhas?
texts.mrk.14.64: Vós ouvistes a blasphemia; que vos parece? E todos o condemnaram como culpado de morte.
texts.mrk.14.65: E alguns começaram a cuspir n’elle, e a cobrir-lhe o rosto, e a dar-lhe punhadas, e a dizer-lhe: Prophetiza. E os servidores davam-lhe bofetadas.
texts.mrk.14.66: E, estando Pedro em baixo, no atrio, chegou uma das creadas do summo sacerdote;
texts.mrk.14.67: E, vendo a Pedro, que se estava aquentando, olhou para elle, e disse: Tu tambem estavas com Jesus Nazareno.
texts.mrk.14.68: Mas elle negou-o, dizendo: Não o conheço, nem sei o que dizes. E saiu fóra ao alpendre, e o gallo cantou.
texts.mrk.14.69: E a creada, vendo-o outra vez, começou a dizer aos que ali estavam: Este é um dos taes.
texts.mrk.14.70: Mas elle o negou outra vez. E pouco depois os que ali estavam disseram outra vez a Pedro: Verdadeiramente tu és um d’elles, porque és tambem galileo, e a tua falla é similhante.
texts.mrk.14.71: E elle começou a imprecar, e a jurar, dizendo: Não conheço esse homem de quem fallaes,
texts.mrk.14.72: E o gallo cantou segunda vez. E Pedro lembrou-se da palavra que Jesus lhe tinha dito: Antes que o gallo cante duas vezes, tres vezes me negarás tu. E, retirando-se d’ali, chorou.
texts.mrk.15.1: E logo ao amanhecer os principaes dos sacerdotes, com os anciãos, e os escribas, e todo o concilio, tiveram conselho; e, amarrando a Jesus, o levaram e entregaram a Pilatos.
texts.mrk.15.2: E Pilatos lhe perguntou: Tu és o Rei dos Judeos? E elle, respondendo, disse-lhe: Tu o dizes.
texts.mrk.15.3: E os principaes dos sacerdotes o accusavam de muitas coisas; porém elle nada respondia.
texts.mrk.15.4: E Pilatos o interrogou outra vez, dizendo: Nada respondes? Vê quantas coisas testificam contra ti.
texts.mrk.15.5: Mas Jesus nada mais respondeu, de maneira que Pilatos se maravilhava.
texts.mrk.15.6: Ora no dia da festa costumava soltar-lhes um preso qualquer que elles pedissem.
texts.mrk.15.7: E havia um chamado Barabbás, que, preso com outros amotinadores, tinha n’um motim commettido uma morte.
texts.mrk.15.8: E a multidão, dando gritos, começou a pedir que fizesse como sempre lhes tinha feito.
texts.mrk.15.9: E Pilatos lhes respondeu, dizendo: Quereis que vos solte o Rei dos Judeos?
texts.mrk.15.10: Porque elle bem sabia que por inveja os principaes dos sacerdotes o tinham entregado.
texts.mrk.15.11: Mas os principaes dos sacerdotes incitaram a multidão para que lhes soltasse antes Barabbás.
texts.mrk.15.12: E Pilatos, respondendo, lhes disse outra vez: Que quereis pois que faça d’aquelle a quem chamaes Rei dos Judeos?
texts.mrk.15.13: E elles tornaram a clamar: Crucifica-o.
texts.mrk.15.14: Mas Pilatos lhes disse: Pois que mal fez? E elles cada vez clamavam mais: Crucifica-o.
texts.mrk.15.15: Porém Pilatos, querendo satisfazer a multidão, soltou-lhes Barabbás, e, açoitado Jesus, o entregou para que fosse crucificado.
texts.mrk.15.16: E os soldados o levaram dentro á sala, que é a da audiência, e convocaram toda a cohorte;
texts.mrk.15.17: E vestiram-n’o de purpura, e, tecendo uma corôa de espinhos, lh’a pozeram na cabeça.
texts.mrk.15.18: E começaram a saudal-o, dizendo: Salve, Rei dos Judeos!
texts.mrk.15.19: E feriram-n’o na cabeça com uma canna, e cuspiram n’elle, e, postos de joelhos, o adoraram.
texts.mrk.15.20: E, havendo-o escarnecido, despiram-lhe a purpura, e o vestiram com os seus proprios vestidos, e o levaram fóra para o crucificar.
texts.mrk.15.21: E constrangeram um certo Simão Cyreneo, pae de Alexandre e de Rufo, que por ali passava, vindo do campo, a que levasse a cruz.
texts.mrk.15.22: E levaram-n’o ao logar do Golgotha, que é, traduzido, logar da Caveira.
texts.mrk.15.23: E deram-lhe a beber vinho com myrrha, mas elle não o tomou.
texts.mrk.15.24: E, havendo-o crucificado, repartiram os seus vestidos, lançando sobre elles sortes, para saber o que cada um levaria.
texts.mrk.15.25: E era a hora terceira, e o crucificaram.
texts.mrk.15.26: E por cima d’elle estava escripta a sua accusação: O REI DOS JUDEOS.
texts.mrk.15.27: E crucificaram com elle dois salteadores, um á sua direita, e outro á esquerda.
texts.mrk.15.28: E cumpriu-se a escriptura que diz: E com os malfeitores foi contado.
texts.mrk.15.29: E os que passavam blasphemavam d’elle, meneando as suas cabeças, e dizendo: Ah! tu que derribas o templo, e em tres dias o edificas,
texts.mrk.15.30: Salva-te a ti mesmo, e desce da cruz.
texts.mrk.15.31: E da mesma maneira tambem os principaes dos sacerdotes, com os escribas, diziam uns para os outros, zombando: Salvou os outros, e não pode salvar-se a si mesmo;
texts.mrk.15.32: O Christo, o Rei d’Israel, desça agora da cruz, para que o vejamos e acreditemos. Tambem os que com elle estavam crucificados o injuriavam.
texts.mrk.15.33: E, chegada a hora sexta, foram feitas trevas sobre toda a terra até á hora nona.
texts.mrk.15.34: E, á hora nona, Jesus exclamou com grande voz, dizendo: Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? que, traduzido, é: Deus meu, Deus meu, porque me desamparaste?
texts.mrk.15.35: E alguns dos que ali estavam, ouvindo isto, diziam: Eis que chama por Elias.
texts.mrk.15.36: E um d’elles correu a encher uma esponja de vinagre, e, pondo-a n’uma canna, deu-lh’o a beber, dizendo: Deixae, vejamos se virá Elias tiral-o.
texts.mrk.15.37: E Jesus, dando um grande brado, expirou.
texts.mrk.15.38: E o véu do templo se rasgou em dois, d’alto a baixo.
texts.mrk.15.39: E o centurião, que estava defronte d’elle, vendo que assim clamando expirára, disse: Verdadeiramente este homem era o Filho de Deus.
texts.mrk.15.40: E tambem ali estavam algumas mulheres, olhando de longe, entre as quaes estavam tambem Maria Magdalena, e Maria, mãe de Thiago, o menor, e de José, e Salomé;
texts.mrk.15.41: As quaes tambem o seguiam, e o serviam, quando estava na Galilea; e muitas outras, que tinham subido com elle a Jerusalem.
texts.mrk.15.42: E, chegada a tarde, porquanto era o dia da preparação, isto é, a vespera do sabbado,
texts.mrk.15.43: Chegou José d’Arimathea, senador honrado, que tambem esperava o reino de Deus, e ousadamente foi a Pilatos, e pediu o corpo de Jesus.
texts.mrk.15.44: E Pilatos se maravilhou de que já estivesse morto. E, chamando o centurião, perguntou-lhe se já havia muito que tinha morrido.
texts.mrk.15.45: E, tendo-se certificado pelo centurião, deu o corpo a José,
texts.mrk.15.46: O qual comprou um lençol fino, e, tirando-o da cruz, o envolveu no lençol, e o depositou n’um sepulchro lavrado n’uma rocha; e revolveu uma pedra para a porta do sepulchro.
texts.mrk.15.47: E Maria Magdalena e Maria mãe de José olhavam onde o punham.
texts.mrk.16.1: E, passado o sabbado, Maria Magdalena, e Maria, mãe de Thiago, e Salomé, compraram aromas para irem ungil-o.
texts.mrk.16.2: E, no primeiro dia da semana, foram ao sepulchro, de manhã cedo, ao nascer do sol;
texts.mrk.16.3: E diziam umas ás outras: Quem nos revolverá a pedra da porta do sepulchro?
texts.mrk.16.4: E, olhando, viram que já a pedra estava revolvida; porque era muito grande.
texts.mrk.16.5: E, entrando no sepulchro, viram um mancebo assentado á direita, vestido de uma roupa comprida, branca; e ficaram espantadas.
texts.mrk.16.6: Porém elle disse-lhes: Não vos assusteis; buscaes a Jesus Nazareno, que foi crucificado; já resuscitou, não está aqui; eis aqui o logar onde o pozeram.
texts.mrk.16.7: Porém ide, dizei a seus discipulos, e a Pedro, que elle vae adiante de vós para a Galilea; ali o vereis, como elle vos disse.
texts.mrk.16.8: E, saindo ellas apressadamente, fugiram do sepulchro, porque estavam possuidas de temor e assombro; e nada diziam a ninguem, porque temiam.
texts.mrk.16.9: E Jesus, tendo resuscitado na manhã do primeiro dia da semana, appareceu primeiramente a Maria Magdalena, da qual tinha expulsado sete demonios.
texts.mrk.16.10: E, partindo ella, annunciou-o áquelles que tinham estado com elle, os quaes estavam tristes, e chorando.
texts.mrk.16.11: E, ouvindo elles que vivia, e que tinha sido visto por ella, não o creram.
texts.mrk.16.12: E depois manifestou-se n’outra fórma a dois d’elles, que iam de caminho para o campo.
texts.mrk.16.13: E, indo estes, annunciaram-n’o aos outros, mas nem ainda estes creram.
texts.mrk.16.14: Finalmente appareceu aos onze, estando elles assentados juntamente, e lançou-lhes em rosto a sua incredulidade e dureza de coração, por não haverem crido nos que o tinham visto já resuscitado.
texts.mrk.16.15: E disse-lhes: Ide por todo o mundo, prégae o evangelho a toda a creatura:
texts.mrk.16.16: Quem crêr e fôr baptizado será salvo; mas quem não crêr será condemnado.
texts.mrk.16.17: E estes signaes seguirão aos que crêrem: Em meu nome expulsarão os demonios; fallarão novas linguas:
texts.mrk.16.18: Pegarão nas serpentes; e, se beberem alguma coisa mortifera, não lhes fará damno algum; e porão as mãos sobre os enfermos, e os sararão.
texts.mrk.16.19: Ora o Senhor, depois de lhes ter fallado, foi recebido acima no céu, e assentou-se á direita de Deus.
texts.mrk.16.20: E elles, tendo partido, prégaram por todas as partes, cooperando com elles o Senhor, e confirmando a palavra com os signaes que se seguiram. Amen.

texts.mrk.1.1: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God;
texts.mrk.1.2: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee;
texts.mrk.1.3: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
texts.mrk.1.4: John was baptizing in the wilderness, and preaching the baptism of repentance, for the remission of sins.
texts.mrk.1.5: And there went out to him all the land of Judea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
texts.mrk.1.6: And John was clothed with camels hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he ate locusts and wild honey;
texts.mrk.1.7: And preached, saying, There cometh after me one mightier than I, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.
texts.mrk.1.8: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
texts.mrk.1.9: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth to Galilee, and was baptized by John in Jordan.
texts.mrk.1.10: And immediately coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him.
texts.mrk.1.11: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
texts.mrk.1.12: And immediately the spirit driveth him into the wilderness.
texts.mrk.1.13: And he was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan: and was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to him.
texts.mrk.1.14: Now after John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
texts.mrk.1.15: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
texts.mrk.1.16: Now as he was walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
texts.mrk.1.17: And Jesus said to them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
texts.mrk.1.18: And immediately they forsook their nets, and followed him.
texts.mrk.1.19: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the boat mending their nets.
texts.mrk.1.20: And immediately he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.
texts.mrk.1.21: And they went into Capernaum; and immediately on the sabbath he entered into the synagogue and taught.
texts.mrk.1.22: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.
texts.mrk.1.23: And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,
texts.mrk.1.24: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
texts.mrk.1.25: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.
texts.mrk.1.26: And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him.
texts.mrk.1.27: And they were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority he commandeth even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.
texts.mrk.1.28: And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region around Galilee.
texts.mrk.1.29: And forthwith, when they had come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
texts.mrk.1.30: But the mother of Simon's wife lay sick with a fever; and forthwith they tell him of her.
texts.mrk.1.31: And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered to them.
texts.mrk.1.32: And at evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with demons.
texts.mrk.1.33: And all the city was gathered at the door.
texts.mrk.1.34: And he healed many that were sick with divers diseases, and cast out many demons; and suffered not the demons to speak, because they knew him.
texts.mrk.1.35: And in the morning, rising a great while before day, he went out and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
texts.mrk.1.36: And Simon, and they that were with him, followed after him.
texts.mrk.1.37: And when they had found him, they said to him, All men seek for thee.
texts.mrk.1.38: And he said to them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for, for this purpose have I come.
texts.mrk.1.39: And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out demons.
texts.mrk.1.40: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying to him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
texts.mrk.1.41: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith to him, I will; be thou clean.
texts.mrk.1.42: And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
texts.mrk.1.43: And he strictly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;
texts.mrk.1.44: And saith to him, See thou say nothing to any man; but go, show thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.
texts.mrk.1.45: But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.
texts.mrk.2.1: And again he entered into Capernaum, after some days; and it was understood that he was in the house.
texts.mrk.2.2: And forthwith many were assembled, so that there was no room to receive them, no not so much as about the door: and he preached the word to them.
texts.mrk.2.3: And they come to him, bringing one sick with the palsy, who was borne by four.
texts.mrk.2.4: And when they could not come nigh to him by reason of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed on which the sick with the palsy lay.
texts.mrk.2.5: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the sick with the palsy, Son, thy sins are forgiven thee.
texts.mrk.2.6: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
texts.mrk.2.7: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?
texts.mrk.2.8: And immediately, when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said to them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?
texts.mrk.2.9: Which is easier, to say to the sick with the palsy, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
texts.mrk.2.10: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, he saith to the sick with the palsy,
texts.mrk.2.11: I say to thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go into thy house.
texts.mrk.2.12: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; so that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.
texts.mrk.2.13: And he went forth again by the sea-side; and all the multitude resorted to him, and he taught them.
texts.mrk.2.14: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alpheus, sitting at the receipt of custom, and said to him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.
texts.mrk.2.15: And it came to pass, that as Jesus sat at table in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples; for there were many, and they followed him.
texts.mrk.2.16: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eating with publicans and sinners, they said to his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners.
texts.mrk.2.17: When Jesus heard it, he saith to them, They that are in health, have no need of a physician, but they that are sick; I came not to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance.
texts.mrk.2.18: And the disciples of John, and of the Pharisees, used to fast: and they come, and say to him, Why do the disciples of John, and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?
texts.mrk.2.19: And Jesus said to them, Can the children of the bride-chamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
texts.mrk.2.20: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then they will fast in those days.
texts.mrk.2.21: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up, taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.
texts.mrk.2.22: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles, else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.
texts.mrk.2.23: And it came to pass, that he went through the corn-fields on the sabbath; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.
texts.mrk.2.24: And the Pharisees said to him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath that which is not lawful?
texts.mrk.2.25: And he said to them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry, he and they that were with him?
texts.mrk.2.26: How he went into the house of God, in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show-bread, which it is not lawful to eat, but for the priests, and gave also to them who were with him?
texts.mrk.2.27: And he said to them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
texts.mrk.2.28: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
texts.mrk.3.1: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there who had a withered hand.
texts.mrk.3.2: And they watched him, to see whether he would heal him on the sabbath; that they might accuse him.
texts.mrk.3.3: And he saith to the man who had the withered hand, Stand forth.
texts.mrk.3.4: And he saith to them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? but they held their peace.
texts.mrk.3.5: And when he had looked around on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
texts.mrk.3.6: And the Pharisees went forth, and immediately took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
texts.mrk.3.7: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judea.
texts.mrk.3.8: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came to him.
texts.mrk.3.9: And he spoke to his disciples, that a small boat should wait on him, because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.
texts.mrk.3.10: For he had healed many; so that they pressed upon him to touch him, as many as had diseases.
texts.mrk.3.11: And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.
texts.mrk.3.12: And he strictly charged them, that they should not make him known.
texts.mrk.3.13: And he goeth up upon a mountain, and calleth to him whom he would: and they came to him.
texts.mrk.3.14: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
texts.mrk.3.15: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out demons.
texts.mrk.3.17: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, (and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, Sons of thunder,)
texts.mrk.3.18: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
texts.mrk.3.19: And Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him: and they went into a house.
texts.mrk.3.20: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
texts.mrk.3.21: And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.
texts.mrk.3.22: And the scribes who came down from Jerusalem, said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the demons he casteth out demons.
texts.mrk.3.23: And he called them to him, and said to them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?
texts.mrk.3.24: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
texts.mrk.3.25: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
texts.mrk.3.26: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.
texts.mrk.3.27: No man can enter into a strong man's house, and seize his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
texts.mrk.3.28: Verily I say to you, All sins shall be forgiven to the sons of men, and any blasphemies with which they shall blaspheme:
texts.mrk.3.29: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never hath forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:
texts.mrk.3.30: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
texts.mrk.3.31: There came then his brethren and his mother, and standing without, they sent to him, calling him.
texts.mrk.3.32: And the multitude sat about him, and they said to him, Behold, thy mother, and thy brethren without seek for thee.
texts.mrk.3.33: And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?
texts.mrk.3.34: And he looked around on them who sat about him, and said, Behold, my mother and my brethren!
texts.mrk.3.35: For whoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
texts.mrk.4.1: And he began again to teach by the sea-side: and there was gathered to him a great multitude, so that he entered into a boat, and sat on the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea, on the land.
texts.mrk.4.2: And he taught them many things by parables, and said to them in his doctrine,
texts.mrk.4.3: Hearken; Behold, a sower went out to sow:
texts.mrk.4.4: And it came to pass as he sowed, some fell by the way-side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it.
texts.mrk.4.5: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth.
texts.mrk.4.6: But when the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
texts.mrk.4.7: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
texts.mrk.4.8: And other fell on good ground, and yielded fruit that sprang up, and increased, and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some a hundred.
texts.mrk.4.9: And he said to them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mrk.4.10: And when he was alone, they that were about him, with the twelve, asked of him the parable.
texts.mrk.4.11: And he said to them, To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but to them that are without, all these things are done in parables:
texts.mrk.4.12: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.
texts.mrk.4.13: And he said to them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?
texts.mrk.4.15: And these are they by the way-side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.
texts.mrk.4.16: And these are they likewise who are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;
texts.mrk.4.17: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they relapse.
texts.mrk.4.18: And these are they who are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,
texts.mrk.4.19: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.
texts.mrk.4.20: And these are they who are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirty-fold, some sixty, and some a hundred.
texts.mrk.4.21: And he said to them, Is a candle brought to be put under a close vessel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?
texts.mrk.4.22: For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither hath any thing been kept secret, but that it should come abroad.
texts.mrk.4.23: If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mrk.4.24: And he said to them, Take heed what ye hear: With the measure which ye give, it shall be measured to you: and to you that hear shall more be given.
texts.mrk.4.25: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.
texts.mrk.4.26: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;
texts.mrk.4.27: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.
texts.mrk.4.28: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of itself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
texts.mrk.4.29: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.
texts.mrk.4.30: And he said, To what shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?
texts.mrk.4.31: It is like a grain of mustard-seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that are in the earth.
texts.mrk.4.32: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under its shade.
texts.mrk.4.33: And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
texts.mrk.4.34: But without a parable he spoke not to them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.
texts.mrk.4.35: And the same day, when the evening was come, he saith to them, Let us pass over to the other side.
texts.mrk.4.36: And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the boat. And there were also with him other small boats.
texts.mrk.4.37: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the boat, so that it was now full.
texts.mrk.4.38: And he was in the hinder part of the boat, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say to him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
texts.mrk.4.39: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, Peace, be still: and the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
texts.mrk.4.40: And he said to them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
texts.mrk.4.41: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
texts.mrk.5.1: And they came over to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
texts.mrk.5.2: And when he had come out of the boat, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
texts.mrk.5.3: Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:
texts.mrk.5.4: For he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
texts.mrk.5.5: And always, night and day, he was on the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.
texts.mrk.5.6: But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshiped him,
texts.mrk.5.7: And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the Most High God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.
texts.mrk.5.8: (For he said to him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.)
texts.mrk.5.9: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
texts.mrk.5.10: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
texts.mrk.5.11: Now there was there nigh to the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.
texts.mrk.5.12: And all the demons besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.
texts.mrk.5.13: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea (they were about two thousand) and were choked in the sea.
texts.mrk.5.14: And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.
texts.mrk.5.15: And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the demon, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
texts.mrk.5.16: And they that saw it told them how it befell him that was possessed with the demon, and also concerning the swine.
texts.mrk.5.17: And they began to pray him to depart out of their borders.
texts.mrk.5.18: And when he had come into the boat, he that had been possessed with the demon prayed him that he might be with him.
texts.mrk.5.19: Yet Jesus suffered him not, but saith to him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
texts.mrk.5.20: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him. And all men wondered.
texts.mrk.5.21: And when Jesus had passed over again in a boat to the other side, much people gathered to him: and he was nigh to the sea.
texts.mrk.5.22: And behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,
texts.mrk.5.23: And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she will live.
texts.mrk.5.24: And Jesus went with him; and many people followed him, and thronged him.
texts.mrk.5.25: And a certain woman who had an issue of blood twelve years,
texts.mrk.5.26: And had suffered many things from many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was not relieved, but rather grew worse,
texts.mrk.5.27: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the crowd behind, and touched his garment.
texts.mrk.5.28: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.
texts.mrk.5.29: And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that infirmity.
texts.mrk.5.30: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the throng, and said, Who touched my clothes?
texts.mrk.5.31: And his disciples said to him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
texts.mrk.5.32: And he looked around, to see her that had done this thing.
texts.mrk.5.33: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
texts.mrk.5.34: And he said to her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be healed of thy infirmity.
texts.mrk.5.35: While he was yet speaking, there came from the ruler of the synagogue's house certain who said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?
texts.mrk.5.36: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith to the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe,
texts.mrk.5.37: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
texts.mrk.5.38: And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.
texts.mrk.5.39: And when he had come in, he saith to them, Why make ye this tumult, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.
texts.mrk.5.40: And they derided him: but when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.
texts.mrk.5.41: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said to her, Talitha cumi: which is, being interpreted, Damsel (I say to thee) arise.
texts.mrk.5.42: And forthwith the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.
texts.mrk.5.43: And he charged them strictly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.
texts.mrk.6.1: And he went out from thence, and came into his own country, and his disciples follow him.
texts.mrk.6.2: And when the sabbath was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given to him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?
texts.mrk.6.3: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Judas, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
texts.mrk.6.4: But Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honor, but in his own country, and among his own kindred, and in his own house.
texts.mrk.6.5: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick persons, and healed them.
texts.mrk.6.6: And he marveled because of their unbelief. And he went around the villages teaching.
texts.mrk.6.7: And he calleth to him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;
texts.mrk.6.8: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no bag, no bread, no money in their purse:
texts.mrk.6.9: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.
texts.mrk.6.10: And he said to them, In whatever place ye enter into a house, there abide till ye depart from that place.
texts.mrk.6.11: And whoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence shake off the dust under your feet, for a testimony against them. Verily I say to you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment, than for that city.
texts.mrk.6.12: And they went out and preached that men should repent.
texts.mrk.6.13: And they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.
texts.mrk.6.14: And king Herod heard of him (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist had risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do show forth themselves in him.
texts.mrk.6.15: Others said, That it is Elijah. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.
texts.mrk.6.16: But when Herod heard of him, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he hath risen from the dead.
texts.mrk.6.17: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife: for he had married her.
texts.mrk.6.18: For John had said to Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife.
texts.mrk.6.19: Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:
texts.mrk.6.20: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just and holy man, and observed him: and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
texts.mrk.6.21: And when a convenient day had come, that Herod on his birth-day made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief men of Galilee;
texts.mrk.6.22: And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod, and them that sat with him, the king said to the damsel, Ask of me whatever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
texts.mrk.6.23: And he swore to her, Whatever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, to the half of my kingdom.
texts.mrk.6.24: And she went forth, and said to her mother, What shall I ask? and she said, The head of John the Baptist.
texts.mrk.6.25: And she came in forthwith with haste to the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou shouldst give me, immediately, in a dish, the head of John the Baptist.
texts.mrk.6.26: And the king was exceeding sorry: yet for his oath's sake, and for their sakes who sat with him, he would not reject her.
texts.mrk.6.27: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
texts.mrk.6.28: And brought his head in a dish, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
texts.mrk.6.29: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
texts.mrk.6.30: And the apostles assembled themselves to Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
texts.mrk.6.31: And he said to them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
texts.mrk.6.32: And they departed into a desert place in a boat privately.
texts.mrk.6.33: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran on foot thither out of all cities, and out went them, and came together to him.
texts.mrk.6.34: And Jesus, when he came out, saw many people, and was moved with compassion towards them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
texts.mrk.6.35: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came to him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:
texts.mrk.6.36: Send them away, that they may go into the country around, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.
texts.mrk.6.37: He answered and said to them, Give ye them to eat. And they say to him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?
texts.mrk.6.38: He saith to them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.
texts.mrk.6.39: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
texts.mrk.6.40: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.
texts.mrk.6.41: And when he had taken the five loaves, and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and broke the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes he divided among them all.
texts.mrk.6.42: And they all ate, and were satisfied.
texts.mrk.6.43: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
texts.mrk.6.44: And they that ate of the loaves, were about five thousand men.
texts.mrk.6.45: And immediately he constrained his disciples to get into the boat, and to go to the other side before to Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
texts.mrk.6.46: And when he had dismissed them, he departed to a mountain to pray.
texts.mrk.6.47: And when evening was come, the boat was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.
texts.mrk.6.48: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary to them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh to them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
texts.mrk.6.49: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out.
texts.mrk.6.50: (For they all saw him, and were troubled.) And immediately he talked with them, and saith to them, Be of good cheer: It is I; be not afraid.
texts.mrk.6.51: And he went up to them into the boat; and the wind ceased: and they were greatly amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.
texts.mrk.6.52: For they considered not the miracle of the loaves; for their heart was hardened.
texts.mrk.6.53: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
texts.mrk.6.54: And when they had come out of the boat forthwith they knew him,
texts.mrk.6.55: And ran through that whole region around, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.
texts.mrk.6.56: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch, if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him, were healed.
texts.mrk.7.1: Then came together to him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, who came from Jerusalem.
texts.mrk.7.2: And when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled (that is to say with unwashed) hands, they found fault.
texts.mrk.7.3: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands often eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.
texts.mrk.7.4: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there are, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, and of brazen vessels, and tables.
texts.mrk.7.5: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?
texts.mrk.7.6: He answered and said to them, Well hath Isaiah prophesied concerning you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoreth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
texts.mrk.7.7: But, in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
texts.mrk.7.8: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
texts.mrk.7.9: And he said to them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition,
texts.mrk.7.10: For Moses said, Honor thy father and thy mother; and, Whoever curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
texts.mrk.7.11: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.
texts.mrk.7.12: And ye suffer him no more to do aught for his father or his mother;
texts.mrk.7.13: Making the word of God of no effect through your traditions, which ye have delivered: and many such like things ye do.
texts.mrk.7.14: And when he had called all the people to him, he said to them, Hearken to me every one of you, and understand.
texts.mrk.7.15: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him, can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.
texts.mrk.7.16: If any man hath ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mrk.7.17: And when he had entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
texts.mrk.7.18: And he saith to them, Are ye so void of understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him.
texts.mrk.7.19: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all kinds of food.
texts.mrk.7.20: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
texts.mrk.7.21: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
texts.mrk.7.22: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness;
texts.mrk.7.23: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
texts.mrk.7.24: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into a house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
texts.mrk.7.25: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
texts.mrk.7.26: (The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation,) and she besought him that he would cast forth the demon out of her daughter.
texts.mrk.7.27: But Jesus said to her, Let the children first be satisfied: for it is not meet to take the children's bread, and to cast it to the dogs.
texts.mrk.7.28: And she answered and said to him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children's crums.
texts.mrk.7.29: And he said to her, For this saying, depart; the demon is gone out of thy daughter.
texts.mrk.7.30: And when she had come to her house, she found the demon had gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.
texts.mrk.7.31: And again, departing from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, he came to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the borders of Decapolis.
texts.mrk.7.32: And they bring to him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.
texts.mrk.7.33: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue.
texts.mrk.7.34: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith to him, Effatha, that is, Be opened.
texts.mrk.7.35: And immediately his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke plain.
texts.mrk.7.36: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them; so much the more a great deal they published it;
texts.mrk.7.37: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well; he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
texts.mrk.8.1: In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples, and saith to them,
texts.mrk.8.2: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:
texts.mrk.8.3: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for some of them came from a distance.
texts.mrk.8.4: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?
texts.mrk.8.5: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
texts.mrk.8.6: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and broke, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they set them before the people.
texts.mrk.8.7: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.
texts.mrk.8.8: So they ate, and were satisfied: and they took up of the fragments that were left, seven baskets.
texts.mrk.8.9: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he dismissed them.
texts.mrk.8.10: And forthwith he entered into a boat with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
texts.mrk.8.11: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, tempting him.
texts.mrk.8.12: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek for a sign? Verily I say to you, There shall no sign be given to this generation.
texts.mrk.8.13: And he left them, and entering into the boat again, departed to the other side.
texts.mrk.8.14: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the boat with them more than one loaf.
texts.mrk.8.15: And he charged them saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.
texts.mrk.8.16: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread.
texts.mrk.8.17: And when Jesus knew it, he saith to them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?
texts.mrk.8.18: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
texts.mrk.8.19: When I divided the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say to him, Twelve.
texts.mrk.8.20: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.
texts.mrk.8.21: And he said to them, How is it that ye do not understand?
texts.mrk.8.22: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man to him, and besought him to touch him.
texts.mrk.8.23: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw aught.
texts.mrk.8.24: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees walking.
texts.mrk.8.25: After that, he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.
texts.mrk.8.26: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.
texts.mrk.8.27: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Cesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying to them, Who do men say that I am?
texts.mrk.8.28: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elijah; and others, One of the prophets,
texts.mrk.8.29: And he saith to them, But who say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith to him, Thou art the Christ.
texts.mrk.8.30: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.
texts.mrk.8.31: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
texts.mrk.8.32: And he spoke that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
texts.mrk.8.33: But when he had turned about, and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savorest not the things that are of God, but the things that are of men.
texts.mrk.8.34: And when he had called the people to him with his disciples also, he said to them, Whoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
texts.mrk.8.35: For whoever will save his life, shall lose it; but whoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel's, the same shall save it.
texts.mrk.8.36: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul:
texts.mrk.8.37: Or what will a man give in exchange for his soul?
texts.mrk.8.38: Whoever therefore shall be ashamed of me, and of my words, in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also will the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
texts.mrk.9.1: And he said to them, Verily I say to you, that there are some of them that stand here who shall not taste death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
texts.mrk.9.2: And after six days, Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up upon a high mountain apart by themselves; and he was transfigured before them.
texts.mrk.9.3: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can whiten them.
texts.mrk.9.4: And there appeared to them Elijah, with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
texts.mrk.9.5: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
texts.mrk.9.6: For he knew not what to say: for they were greatly terrified.
texts.mrk.9.7: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
texts.mrk.9.8: And suddenly, when they had looked around, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
texts.mrk.9.9: And as they came down from the mountain, he charged them that they should tell no man what things they had seen, till the Son of man were risen from the dead.
texts.mrk.9.10: And they kept that saying with themselves, questioning one with another what the rising from the dead should mean.
texts.mrk.9.11: And they asked him, saying, Why say the scribes that Elijah must first come?
texts.mrk.9.12: And he answered and told them, Elijah verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written concerning the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at naught.
texts.mrk.9.13: But I say to you, that Elijah is indeed come, and they have done to him whatever they pleased, as it is written concerning him.
texts.mrk.9.14: And when he came to his disciples, he saw a great multitude about them, and the scribes questioning with them.
texts.mrk.9.15: And immediately all the people, when they beheld him, were greatly amazed, and running to him, saluted him.
texts.mrk.9.16: And he asked the scribes, What question ye with them?
texts.mrk.9.17: And one of the multitude answered and said, Master, I have brought to thee my son, who hath a dumb spirit;
texts.mrk.9.18: And wherever he taketh him, he teareth him; and he foameth and gnasheth with his teeth, and pineth away; and I spoke to thy disciples that they should cast him out, and they could not.
texts.mrk.9.19: He answered him, and saith, O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you, how long shall I suffer you? bring him to me.
texts.mrk.9.20: And they brought him to him: and when he saw him, immediately the spirit tore him; and he fell on the ground, and wallowed, foaming.
texts.mrk.9.21: And he asked his father, How long is it since this came to him? and he said, From a child.
texts.mrk.9.22: And often it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters to destroy him: but if thou canst do any thing, have compassion on us, and help us.
texts.mrk.9.23: Jesus said to him, If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
texts.mrk.9.24: And immediately the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou my unbelief.
texts.mrk.9.25: When Jesus saw that the people came running together, he rebuked the foul spirit, saying to him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
texts.mrk.9.26: And the spirit cried, and rent him severely, and came out of him: and he was as one dead; so that many said, He is dead.
texts.mrk.9.27: But Jesus took him by the hand, and lifted him up; and he arose.
texts.mrk.9.28: And when he had come into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast him out?
texts.mrk.9.29: And he said to them, This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.
texts.mrk.9.30: And they departed thence, and passed through Galilee; and he would not that any man should know it.
texts.mrk.9.31: For he taught his disciples, and said to them, The Son of man is delivered into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and after that he is killed, he will rise the third day.
texts.mrk.9.32: But they understood not that saying, and were afraid to ask him.
texts.mrk.9.33: And he came to Capernaum: and being in the house, he asked them, What was it that ye disputed among yourselves by the way?
texts.mrk.9.34: But they held their peace: for by the way they had disputed among themselves, who should be the greatest.
texts.mrk.9.35: And he sat down, and called the twelve, and saith to them, If any man desireth to be first, the same shall be last of all, and servant of all.
texts.mrk.9.36: And he took a child, and set him in the midst of them: and when he had taken him in his arms, he said to them,
texts.mrk.9.37: Whoever shall receive one of such children in my name, receiveth me: and whoever shall receive me, receiveth not me, but him that sent me.
texts.mrk.9.38: And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out demons in thy name, and he followeth not us; and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.
texts.mrk.9.39: But Jesus said, Forbid him not; for there is no man who shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.
texts.mrk.9.40: For he that is not against us, is on our part.
texts.mrk.9.41: For whoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in my name, because ye belong to Christ, verily I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.
texts.mrk.9.42: And whoever shall cause one of these little ones that believe in me, to fall into sin, it is better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he were cast into the sea.
texts.mrk.9.43: And if thy hand causeth thee to fall into sin, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:
texts.mrk.9.44: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
texts.mrk.9.45: And if thy foot causeth thee to fall into sin, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter halt into life, than having two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:
texts.mrk.9.46: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
texts.mrk.9.47: And if thy eye causeth thee to fall into sin, pluck it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, than having two eyes, to be cast into hell-fire.
texts.mrk.9.48: Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.
texts.mrk.9.49: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.
texts.mrk.9.50: Salt is good: but if the salt hath lost its saltness, with what will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and have peace one with another.
texts.mrk.10.1: And he arose from thence, and cometh into the borders of Judea, by the further side of Jordan: and the people resort to him again; and, as he was accustomed, he taught them again.
