texts.mrk.10.2: And the Pharisees came to him, and asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife? tempting him.
texts.mrk.10.3: And he answered and said to them, What did Moses command you?
texts.mrk.10.4: And they said, Moses suffered to write a bill of divorcement, and to put her away.
texts.mrk.10.5: And Jesus answered and said to them, For the hardness of your heart, he wrote you this precept.
texts.mrk.10.6: But from the beginning of the creation, God made them male and female.
texts.mrk.10.7: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and cleave to his wife;
texts.mrk.10.8: And they two shall be one flesh: so then they are no more two, but one flesh.
texts.mrk.10.9: What therefore God hath joined together, let not man separate.
texts.mrk.10.10: And in the house his disciples asked him again of the same matter.
texts.mrk.10.11: And he saith to them, Whoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.
texts.mrk.10.12: And if a woman shall put away her husband, and be married to another, she committeth adultery.
texts.mrk.10.13: And they brought young children to him, that he should touch them; and his disciples rebuked those that brought them.
texts.mrk.10.14: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said to them, Suffer the little children to come to me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
texts.mrk.10.15: Verily I say to you, Whoever shall not receive the kingdom of God, as a little child, he shall not enter it.
texts.mrk.10.16: And he took them up in his arms, put his hands upon them, and blessed them.
texts.mrk.10.17: And when he had gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
texts.mrk.10.18: And Jesus said to him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good, but one, that is God.
texts.mrk.10.19: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honor thy father and mother.
texts.mrk.10.20: And he answered and said to him, Master, all these have I observed from my youth.
texts.mrk.10.21: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said to him, One thing thou lackest: go, sell whatever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come, take up the cross, and follow me.
texts.mrk.10.22: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.
texts.mrk.10.23: And Jesus looked around, and saith to his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
texts.mrk.10.24: And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith to them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
texts.mrk.10.25: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.mrk.10.26: And they were astonished beyond measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved?
texts.mrk.10.27: And Jesus looking upon them, saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.
texts.mrk.10.28: Then Peter began to say to him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee.
texts.mrk.10.29: Jesus answered and said, Verily I say to you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's,
texts.mrk.10.30: But he shall receive a hundred-fold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come, eternal life.
texts.mrk.10.31: But many that are first shall be last; and the last first.
texts.mrk.10.32: And they were in the way, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus went before them: and they were amazed; and as they followed, they were afraid. And he took again the twelve, and began to tell them what things should happen to him,
texts.mrk.10.33: Saying, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem; and the Son of man will be delivered to the chief priests, and to the scribes; and they will condemn him to death, and will deliver him to the Gentiles;
texts.mrk.10.34: And they will mock him, and will scourge him, and will spit upon him, and will kill him: and the third day he will rise again.
texts.mrk.10.35: And James and John the sons of Zebedee come to him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatever we shall desire.
texts.mrk.10.36: And he said to them, What would ye that I should do for you?
texts.mrk.10.37: They said to him, Grant to us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory.
texts.mrk.10.38: But Jesus said to them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?
texts.mrk.10.39: And they said to him, We can. And Jesus said to them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of: and with the baptism that I am baptized with shalt ye be baptized;
texts.mrk.10.40: But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand, is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared.
texts.mrk.10.41: And when the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John.
texts.mrk.10.42: But Jesus called them, and saith to them, Ye know that they who are accounted to rule over the Gentiles, exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them.
texts.mrk.10.43: But so it shall not be among you: but whoever will be great among you, shall be your minister:
texts.mrk.10.44: And whoever of you will be the chief, shall be servant of all.
texts.mrk.10.45: For even the son of man came not to be ministered to, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
texts.mrk.10.46: And they came to Jericho: and as he went out of Jericho with his disciples, and a great number of people, blind Bartimeus, the son of Timeus, sat by the highway-side begging.
texts.mrk.10.47: And when he heard that it was Jesus of Nazareth, he began to cry out, and say, Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.mrk.10.48: And many charged him that he should hold his peace: but he cried the more a great deal, Thou son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.mrk.10.49: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called: and they call the blind man, saying to him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.
texts.mrk.10.50: And he, casting away his garment, rose, and came to Jesus.
texts.mrk.10.51: And Jesus answered and said to him, What wilt thou that I should do to thee? The blind man said to him, Lord, that I may receive my sight.
texts.mrk.10.52: And Jesus said to him, Go, thy faith hath made thee whole. And immediately he received his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.
texts.mrk.11.1: And when they came nigh to Jerusalem, to Bethphage, and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, he sendeth forth two of his disciples,
texts.mrk.11.2: And saith to them, Go into the village over against you: and as soon as ye have entered into it, ye shall find a colt tied, on which never man sat; loose him, and bring him.
texts.mrk.11.3: And if any man shall say to you, Why do ye this? say ye that the Lord hath need of him; and immediately he will send him hither.
texts.mrk.11.4: And they went, and found the colt tied by the door without, in a place where two ways met; and they loose him.
texts.mrk.11.5: And certain of them that stood there, said to them, What do ye, loosing the colt?
texts.mrk.11.6: And they said to them even as Jesus had commanded; and they let them go.
texts.mrk.11.7: And they brought the colt to Jesus, and cast their garments on him; and he sat upon him.
texts.mrk.11.8: And many spread their garments in the way: and others cut down branches off trees, and strewed them in the way.
texts.mrk.11.9: And they that went before, and they that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna: Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
texts.mrk.11.10: Blessed be the kingdom of our Father David, that cometh in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest.
texts.mrk.11.11: And Jesus entered into Jerusalem, and into the temple: and when he had looked round upon all things, it being now evening, he went out to Bethany, with the twelve.
texts.mrk.11.12: And on the morrow, when they had come from Bethany, he was hungry,
texts.mrk.11.13: And seeing a fig-tree afar off, having leaves, he came, if haply he might find any thing on it: and when he came to it, he found nothing but leaves: for the time of figs had not yet come.
texts.mrk.11.14: And Jesus answered and said to it, Let no man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever. And his disciples heard it.
texts.mrk.11.15: And they come to Jerusalem: and Jesus went into the temple, and began to cast out them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money-changers, and the seats of them that sold doves;
texts.mrk.11.16: And would not suffer that any man should carry any vessel through the temple.
texts.mrk.11.17: And he taught, saying to them, Is it not written, My house shall be called by all nations the house of prayer? but ye have made it a den of thieves.
texts.mrk.11.18: And the scribes and chief priests heard it, and sought how they might destroy him: for they feared him, because all the people were astonished at his doctrine.
texts.mrk.11.19: And when evening had come, he went out of the city.
texts.mrk.11.20: And in the morning, as they passed by, they saw the fig-tree dried up from the roots.
texts.mrk.11.21: And Peter calling to remembrance, saith to him, Master, behold, the fig-tree which thou cursedst is withered.
texts.mrk.11.22: And Jesus answering, saith to them, Have faith in God.
texts.mrk.11.23: For verily I say to you, that whoever shall say to this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; and shall not doubt in his heart, but shall believe that the things which he saith shall come to pass; he shall have whatever he saith.
texts.mrk.11.24: Therefore I say to you, Whatever things ye desire when ye pray, believe that ye receive them, and ye shall have them.
texts.mrk.11.25: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have aught against any: that your Father also who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.
texts.mrk.11.26: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your trespasses.
texts.mrk.11.27: And they come again to Jerusalem: and as he was walking in the temple, there come to him the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders,
texts.mrk.11.28: And say to him, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority to do these things?
texts.mrk.11.29: And Jesus answered and said to them, I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mrk.11.30: The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or from men? answer me.
texts.mrk.11.31: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did ye not believe him?
texts.mrk.11.32: But if we shall say, from men; they feared the people: for all men counted John that he was a prophet indeed.
texts.mrk.11.33: And they answered and said to Jesus, We cannot tell. And Jesus answering saith to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mrk.12.1: And he began to speak to them by parables. A certain man planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and digged a place for the wine-vat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country.
texts.mrk.12.2: And at the season he sent to the husbandmen a servant, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.
texts.mrk.12.3: And they caught him, and beat him and sent him away empty.
texts.mrk.12.4: And again, he sent to them another servant: and at him they cast stones, and wounded him in the head, and sent him away shamefully handled.
texts.mrk.12.5: And again he sent another; and him they killed, and many others; beating some, and killing some.
texts.mrk.12.6: Having yet therefore one son, his well-beloved, he sent him also last to them, saying, They will reverence my son.
texts.mrk.12.7: But those husbandmen said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.
texts.mrk.12.8: And they took him, and killed him, and cast him out of the vineyard.
texts.mrk.12.9: What therefore will the Lord of the vineyard do? he will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard to others.
texts.mrk.12.10: And have ye not read this scripture; The stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner:
texts.mrk.12.11: This was the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes?
texts.mrk.12.12: And they sought to lay hold on him, but feared the people; for they knew that he had spoken the parable against them: and they left him, and departed.
texts.mrk.12.13: And they sent to him certain of the Pharisees, and of the Herodians, to catch him in his words.
texts.mrk.12.14: And when they had come, they say to him, Master, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man: for thou regardest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God in truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Cesar, or not?
texts.mrk.12.15: Shall we give, or shall we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, Why tempt ye me? bring me a penny, that I may see it.
texts.mrk.12.16: And they brought it: and he saith to them, Whose is this image and superscription? And they said to him, Cesar's.
texts.mrk.12.17: And Jesus answering, said to them, Render to Cesar the things that are Cesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they wondered at him.
texts.mrk.12.18: Then come to him the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection; and they asked him, saying,
texts.mrk.12.19: Master, Moses wrote to us, If a man's brother shall die, and leave his wife, and leave no children, that his brother should take his wife, and raise seed to his brother.
texts.mrk.12.20: Now there were seven brothers: and the first took a wife, and dying left no seed.
texts.mrk.12.21: And the second took her, and died, neither left he any seed: and the third likewise.
texts.mrk.12.22: And the seven had her, and left no seed: last of all the woman died also.
texts.mrk.12.23: In the resurrection therefore, when they shall rise, whose wife shall she be of them? for the seven had her for a wife.
texts.mrk.12.24: And Jesus answering, said to them, Do ye not therefore err, because ye know not the scriptures, neither the power of God?
texts.mrk.12.25: For when they shall rise from the dead, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels who are in heaven.
texts.mrk.12.26: And concerning the dead that they rise; have ye not read in the book of Moses, how in the bush God spoke to him, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
texts.mrk.12.27: He is not the God of the dead, but the God of the living: ye therefore do greatly err.
texts.mrk.12.28: And one of the scribes came, and having heard them reasoning together, and perceiving that he had answered them well, asked him, Which is the first commandment of all?
texts.mrk.12.29: And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord.
texts.mrk.12.30: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment.
texts.mrk.12.31: And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself: there is no other commandment greater than these.
texts.mrk.12.32: And the scribe said to him, Well, Master, thou hast said the truth: for there is one God; and there is no other but he.
texts.mrk.12.33: And to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more than all whole burnt-offerings and sacrifices.
texts.mrk.12.34: And when Jesus saw that he answered discreetly, he said to him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no man after that durst ask him any question.
texts.mrk.12.35: And Jesus answered and said, while he taught in the temple, How say the scribes that Christ is the son of David?
texts.mrk.12.36: For David himself said by the Holy Spirit, The LORD said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thy enemies thy footstool.
texts.mrk.12.37: David therefore himself calleth him Lord, and whence is he then his son? and the common people heard him gladly.
texts.mrk.12.38: And he said to them in his doctrine, Beware of the scribes, who love to go in long clothing, and love salutations in the market-places,
texts.mrk.12.39: And the chief seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost rooms at feasts:
texts.mrk.12.40: Who devour widows' houses, and for a pretense make long prayers: these shall receive greater damnation.
texts.mrk.12.41: And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.
texts.mrk.12.42: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
texts.mrk.12.43: And he called his disciples, and saith to them, Verily I say to you, that this poor widow hath cast in more, than all they who have cast into the treasury.
texts.mrk.12.44: For all they cast in of their abundance: but she of her want cast in all that she had, even all her living.
texts.mrk.13.1: And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples saith to him, Master, see what manner of stones, and what buildings are here!
texts.mrk.13.2: And Jesus answering said to him, Seest thou these great buildings? there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
texts.mrk.13.3: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, over against the temple, Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, asked him privately,
texts.mrk.13.4: Tell us, when will these things be? and what will be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled?
texts.mrk.13.5: And Jesus answering them, began to say, Take heed lest any man deceive you:
texts.mrk.13.6: For many will come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and will deceive many.
texts.mrk.13.7: And when ye shall hear of wars, and rumors of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end will not be yet.
texts.mrk.13.8: For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there will be earthquakes in divers places, and there will be famines, and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.
texts.mrk.13.9: But take heed to yourselves: for they will deliver you up to councils; and in the synagogues ye will be beaten: and ye will be brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them.
texts.mrk.13.10: And the gospel must first be published among all nations.
texts.mrk.13.11: But when they shall lead you, and deliver you up, be not anxious beforehand what ye shall speak, neither do ye premeditate: but whatever shall be given you in that hour, that speak ye: for it is not ye that speak, but the Holy Spirit.
texts.mrk.13.12: Now the brother will betray the brother to death, and the father the son: and children will rise up against their parents, and will cause them to be put to death.
texts.mrk.13.13: And ye will be hated by all men for my name's sake: but he that shall endure to the end, the same shall be saved.
texts.mrk.13.14: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing where it ought not, (let him that readeth understand) then let them that are in Judea flee to the mountains:
texts.mrk.13.15: And let him that is on the house-top not go down into the house, neither enter it, to take any thing out of his house:
texts.mrk.13.16: And let him that is in the field not turn back again to take up his garment.
texts.mrk.13.17: But woe to them that are with child, and to them that nurse infants in those days.
texts.mrk.13.18: And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter.
texts.mrk.13.19: For in those days shall be affliction, such as hath not been from the beginning of the creation which God created to this time, neither shall be.
texts.mrk.13.20: And except the Lord had shortened those days, no flesh would be saved: but for the elect's sake, whom he hath chosen, he hath shortened the days.
texts.mrk.13.21: And then, if any man shall say to you, Lo, here is Christ; or lo, he is there; believe him not.
texts.mrk.13.22: For false Christs, and false prophets will rise, and will show signs and wonders, to seduce, if it were possible, even the elect.
texts.mrk.13.23: But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things.
texts.mrk.13.24: But in those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light,
texts.mrk.13.25: And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken.
texts.mrk.13.26: And then they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory.
texts.mrk.13.27: And then he will send his angels, and will assemble his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.
texts.mrk.13.28: Now learn a parable of the fig-tree: When its branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is near:
texts.mrk.13.29: So ye in like manner, when ye shall see these things come to pass, know that it is nigh, even at the doors.
texts.mrk.13.30: Verily I say to you, that this generation shall not pass, till all these things shall be done.
texts.mrk.13.31: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.
texts.mrk.13.32: But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father.
texts.mrk.13.33: Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.
texts.mrk.13.34: For the son of man is as a man taking a long journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work; and commanded the porter to watch.
texts.mrk.13.35: Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at evening, or at midnight, or at the cock-crowing, or in the morning:
texts.mrk.13.36: Lest coming suddenly, he should find you sleeping.
texts.mrk.13.37: And what I say to you, I say to all, Watch.
texts.mrk.14.1: After two days was the feast of the passover, and of unleavened bread: and the chief priests, and the scribes, sought how they might take him by craft, and put him to death.
texts.mrk.14.2: But they said, Not on the feast-day, lest there should be an uproar of the people.
texts.mrk.14.3: And being in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he sat at table, there came a woman having an alabaster box of ointment of spikenard, very precious; and she broke the box, and poured it on his head.
texts.mrk.14.4: And there were some that had indignation within themselves, and said, Why was this waste of the ointment made?
texts.mrk.14.5: For it might have been sold for more than three hundred pence, and have been given to the poor. And they murmured against her.
texts.mrk.14.6: And Jesus said, Let her alone; why trouble ye her? she hath wrought a good work on me.
texts.mrk.14.7: For ye have the poor with you always, and whenever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.
texts.mrk.14.8: She hath done what she could: she is come beforehand to anoint my body to the burying.
texts.mrk.14.9: Verily I say to you, Wherever this gospel shall be preached throughout the whole world, this also that she hath done shall be spoken of, for a memorial of her.
texts.mrk.14.10: And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests, to betray him to them.
texts.mrk.14.11: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him money. And he sought how he might conveniently betray him.
texts.mrk.14.12: And the first day of unleavened bread, when they killed the passover, his disciples said to him, Where wilt thou that we go and prepare, that thou mayest eat the passover?
texts.mrk.14.13: And he sendeth two of his disciples, and saith to them, Go ye into the city, and there shall meet you a man bearing a pitcher of water: follow him.
texts.mrk.14.14: And wherever he shall go in, say ye to the master of the house, The Master saith, Where is the guest-chamber, where I may eat the passover with my disciples?
texts.mrk.14.15: And he will show you a large upper room furnished and prepared: there make ready for us.
texts.mrk.14.16: And his disciples went, and came into the city, and found as he had said to them: and they made ready the passover.
texts.mrk.14.17: And in the evening he cometh with the twelve.
texts.mrk.14.18: And as they sat, and were eating, Jesus said, Verily I say to you, One of you who eateth with me, will betray me.
texts.mrk.14.19: And they began to be sorrowful, and to say to him one by one, Is it I? and another said, Is it I?
texts.mrk.14.20: And he answered and said to them, It is one of the twelve that dippeth with me in the dish.
texts.mrk.14.21: The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written concerning him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had never been born.
texts.mrk.14.22: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and blessed, and broke it, and gave to them, and said, Take, eat: this is my body.
texts.mrk.14.23: And he took the cup, and when he had given thanks, he gave it to them: and they all drank of it.
texts.mrk.14.24: And he said to them, This is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many.
texts.mrk.14.25: Verily I say to you, I will drink no more of the fruit of the vine, until that day that I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
texts.mrk.14.26: And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the mount of Olives.
texts.mrk.14.27: And Jesus saith to them, All ye will be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.
texts.mrk.14.28: But after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.
texts.mrk.14.29: But Peter said to him, Although all shall be offended, yet will not I.
texts.mrk.14.30: And Jesus saith to him, Verily I say to thee, that this day, even in this night, before the cock shall crow twice, thou wilt deny me thrice.
texts.mrk.14.31: But he spoke the more vehemently, If I should die with thee, I will not deny thee in any wise. Likewise also said they all.
texts.mrk.14.32: And they came to a place which was named Gethsemane: and he saith to his disciples, Sit ye here, while I shall pray.
texts.mrk.14.33: And he taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and began to be greatly amazed, and to be very heavy;
texts.mrk.14.34: And saith to them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful to death: tarry ye here, and watch.
texts.mrk.14.35: And he went forward a little, and fell on the ground, and prayed that, If it were possible, the hour might pass from him.
texts.mrk.14.36: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible to thee; take away this cup from me: nevertheless, not what I will, but what thou wilt.
texts.mrk.14.37: And he cometh, and findeth them sleeping, and saith to Peter, Simon, sleepest thou? couldst not thou watch one hour?
texts.mrk.14.38: Watch ye and pray, lest ye enter into temptation. The spirit truly is ready, but the flesh is weak.
texts.mrk.14.39: And again he went away, and prayed, and spoke the same words.
texts.mrk.14.40: And when he returned, he found them asleep again (for their eyes were heavy:) neither knew they what to answer him.
texts.mrk.14.41: And he cometh the third time, and saith to them, Sleep on now, and take your rest: it is enough, the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners.
texts.mrk.14.42: Rise, let us go; lo, he that betrayeth me is at hand.
texts.mrk.14.43: And immediately while he was yet speaking, cometh Judas, one of the twelve, and with him a great multitude with swords and staffs, from the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders.
texts.mrk.14.44: And he that betrayed him, had given them a token, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he; take him, and lead him away safely.
texts.mrk.14.45: And as soon as he was come, he goeth immediately to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him.
texts.mrk.14.46: And they laid their hands on him, and took him.
texts.mrk.14.47: And one of them that stood by drew a sword, and smote a servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
texts.mrk.14.48: And Jesus answered and said to them, Have ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staffs to take me?
texts.mrk.14.49: I was daily with you in the temple, teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.
texts.mrk.14.50: And they all forsook him, and fled.
texts.mrk.14.51: And there followed him a certain young man, having a linen cloth cast about his naked body; and the young men laid hold on him.
texts.mrk.14.52: And he left the linen cloth, and fled from them naked.
texts.mrk.14.53: And they led Jesus away to the high priest: and with him were assembled all the chief priests, and the elders and the scribes.
texts.mrk.14.54: And Peter followed him at a distance, even into the palace of the high priest: and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.
texts.mrk.14.55: And the chief priests, and all the council sought for testimony against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.
texts.mrk.14.56: For many bore false testimony against him, but their testimony agreed not together.
texts.mrk.14.57: And there arose certain, and bore false testimony against him, saying,
texts.mrk.14.58: We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.
texts.mrk.14.59: But neither so did their testimony agree together.
texts.mrk.14.60: And the high priest stood up in the midst, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these testify against thee?
texts.mrk.14.61: But he held his peace, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said to him, Art thou the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?
texts.mrk.14.62: And Jesus said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
texts.mrk.14.63: Then the high priest rent his clothes, and saith, What need we any further witnesses?
texts.mrk.14.64: Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.
texts.mrk.14.65: And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say to him, Prophesy: and the servants struck him with the palms of their hands.
texts.mrk.14.66: And as Peter was below in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest:
texts.mrk.14.67: And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.
texts.mrk.14.68: But he denied, saying, I know not, neither do I understand what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crowed.
texts.mrk.14.69: And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is one of them.
texts.mrk.14.70: And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art one of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech agreeth thereto.
texts.mrk.14.71: But he began to curse and to swear, saying, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
texts.mrk.14.72: And the second time the cock crowed. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said to him, Before the cock shall crow twice, thou wilt deny me thrice. And when he thought thereon, he wept.
texts.mrk.15.1: And forthwith in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him to Pilate.
texts.mrk.15.2: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering, said to him, Thou sayest it.
texts.mrk.15.3: And the chief priests accused him of many things: but he answered nothing.
texts.mrk.15.4: And Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they testify against thee.
texts.mrk.15.5: But Jesus yet answered nothing: so that Pilate marveled.
texts.mrk.15.6: Now at that feast he released to them one prisoner, whom they desired.
texts.mrk.15.7: And there was one named Barabbas, who lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.
texts.mrk.15.8: And the multitude crying aloud, began to desire him to do as he had ever done to them.
texts.mrk.15.9: But Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release to you the King of the Jews?
texts.mrk.15.10: (For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.)
texts.mrk.15.11: But the chief priests moved the people that he should rather release Barabbas to them.
texts.mrk.15.12: And Pilate answered, and said again to them, What will ye then that I shall do to him whom ye call the King of the Jews?
texts.mrk.15.13: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
texts.mrk.15.14: Then Pilate said to them, Why, what evil hath he done? And they cried out the more exceedingly, Crucify him.
texts.mrk.15.15: And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas to them, and having scourged Jesus, delivered him to be crucified.
texts.mrk.15.16: And the soldiers led him away into the hall, called Pretorium; and they call together the whole band;
texts.mrk.15.17: And they clothed him with purple, and platted a crown of thorns, and put it about his head,
texts.mrk.15.18: And began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!
texts.mrk.15.19: And they struck him on the head with a reed, and spit upon him, and bowing their knees, worshiped him.
texts.mrk.15.20: And when they had mocked him, they took off the purple from him, and put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.
texts.mrk.15.21: And they constrain one Simon, a Cyrenian, who was passing by, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross.
texts.mrk.15.22: And they bring him to the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.
texts.mrk.15.23: And they gave him to drink, wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.
texts.mrk.15.24: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.
texts.mrk.15.25: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
texts.mrk.15.26: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
texts.mrk.15.27: And with him they crucify two thieves, the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
texts.mrk.15.28: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.
texts.mrk.15.29: And they that passed by, railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,
texts.mrk.15.30: Save thyself, and come down from the cross.
texts.mrk.15.31: Likewise also the chief priests mocking, said among themselves with the scribes, He saved others, himself he cannot save.
texts.mrk.15.32: Let Christ the king of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him, reviled him.
texts.mrk.15.33: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land, until the ninth hour.
texts.mrk.15.34: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama, sabacthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
texts.mrk.15.35: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elijah.
texts.mrk.15.36: And one ran and filled a sponge full of vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elijah will come to take him down.
texts.mrk.15.37: And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and expired.
texts.mrk.15.38: And the vail of the temple was rent in two, from the top to the bottom.
texts.mrk.15.39: And when the centurion who stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and expired, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
texts.mrk.15.40: There were also women looking on at a distance, among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger, and of Joses, and Salome;
texts.mrk.15.41: Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered to him; and many other women who came with him to Jerusalem.
texts.mrk.15.42: And now, when the evening was come, (because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath)
texts.mrk.15.43: Joseph of Arimathea, an honorable counselor, who also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly to Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.
texts.mrk.15.44: And Pilate wondered if he was already dead: and calling the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.
texts.mrk.15.45: And when he knew it from the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
texts.mrk.15.46: And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulcher which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone to the door of the sepulcher.
texts.mrk.15.47: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses, beheld where he was laid.
texts.mrk.16.1: And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.
texts.mrk.16.2: And very early in the morning, the first day of the week, they came to the sepulcher at the rising of the sun:
texts.mrk.16.3: And they said among themselves, Who shall roll away for us the stone from the door of the sepulcher?
texts.mrk.16.4: (And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away) for it was very great.
texts.mrk.16.5: And entering into the sepulcher, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were frightened.
texts.mrk.16.6: And he saith to them, Be not frightened: ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, who was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him:
texts.mrk.16.7: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said to you.
texts.mrk.16.8: And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulcher; for they trembled, and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man; for they were afraid.
texts.mrk.16.9: Now when Jesus was risen early, the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven demons.
texts.mrk.16.10: And she went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
texts.mrk.16.11: And they, when they had heard that he was alive, and had been seen by her, believed not.
texts.mrk.16.12: After that, he appeared in another form to two of them, as they were walking and going into the country.
texts.mrk.16.13: And they went and told it to the residue: neither believed they them.
texts.mrk.16.14: Afterward he appeared to the eleven, as they sat at table, and upbraided them with their unbelief, and hardness of heart, because they believed not them who had seen him after he was risen.
texts.mrk.16.15: And he said to them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
texts.mrk.16.16: He that believeth and is baptized, shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
texts.mrk.16.17: And these signs shall follow them that believe: In my name shall they cast out demons; they shall speak in new languages;
texts.mrk.16.18: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.
texts.mrk.16.19: So then after the Lord had spoken to them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God.
texts.mrk.16.20: And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.

texts.mrk.1.1: Beginning of the glad tidings of Jesus Christ, Son of God;
texts.mrk.1.2: as it is written in [Isaiah] the prophet, Behold, *I* send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way.
texts.mrk.1.3: Voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of [the] Lord, make his paths straight.
texts.mrk.1.4: There came John baptising in the wilderness, and preaching [the] baptism of repentance for remission of sins.
texts.mrk.1.5: And there went out to him all the district of Judaea, and all they of Jerusalem, and were baptised by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
texts.mrk.1.6: And John was clothed in camel's hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins, and ate locusts and wild honey.
texts.mrk.1.7: And he preached, saying, There comes he that is mightier than I after me, the thong of whose sandals I am not fit to stoop down and unloose.
texts.mrk.1.8: *I* indeed have baptised you with water, but *he* shall baptise you with [the] Holy Spirit.
texts.mrk.1.9: And it came to pass in those days [that] Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptised by John at the Jordan.
texts.mrk.1.10: And straightway going up from the water, he saw the heavens parting asunder, and the Spirit, as a dove, descending upon him.
texts.mrk.1.11: And there came a voice out of the heavens: *Thou* art my beloved Son, in thee I have found my delight.
texts.mrk.1.12: And immediately the Spirit drives him out into the wilderness.
texts.mrk.1.13: And he was in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan, and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered to him.
texts.mrk.1.14: But after John was delivered up, Jesus came into Galilee preaching the glad tidings of the kingdom of God,
texts.mrk.1.15: and saying, The time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God has drawn nigh; repent and believe in the glad tidings.
texts.mrk.1.16: And walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon, and Andrew, [Simon's] brother, casting out a net in the sea, for they were fishers.
texts.mrk.1.17: And Jesus said to them, Come after me, and I will make you become fishers of men;
texts.mrk.1.18: and straightway leaving their trawl-nets they followed him.
texts.mrk.1.19: And going on thence a little, he saw James the [son] of Zebedee, and John his brother, and these [were] in the ship repairing the trawl-nets;
texts.mrk.1.20: and straightway he called them; and leaving their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, they went away after him.
texts.mrk.1.21: And they go into Capernaum. And straightway on the sabbath he entered into the synagogue and taught.
texts.mrk.1.22: And they were astonished at his doctrine, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
texts.mrk.1.23: And there was in their synagogue a man [possessed] by an unclean spirit, and he cried out
texts.mrk.1.24: saying, Eh! what have we to do with thee, Jesus, Nazarene? Art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the holy one of God.
texts.mrk.1.25: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace and come out of him.
texts.mrk.1.26: And the unclean spirit, having torn him, and uttered a cry with a loud voice, came out of him.
texts.mrk.1.27: And all were amazed, so that they questioned together among themselves, saying, What is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.
texts.mrk.1.28: And his fame went out straightway into the whole region of Galilee around.
texts.mrk.1.29: And straightway going out of the synagogue, they came with James and John into the house of Simon and Andrew.
texts.mrk.1.30: And the mother-in-law of Simon lay in a fever. And straightway they speak to him about her.
texts.mrk.1.31: And he went up to [her] and raised her up, having taken her by the hand, and straightway the fever left her, and she served them.
texts.mrk.1.32: But evening being come, when the sun had gone down, they brought to him all that were suffering, and those possessed by demons;
texts.mrk.1.33: and the whole city was gathered together at the door.
texts.mrk.1.34: And he healed many suffering from various diseases; and he cast out many demons, and did not suffer the demons to speak because they knew him.
texts.mrk.1.35: And rising in the morning long before day, he went out and went away into a desert place, and there prayed.
texts.mrk.1.36: And Simon and those with him went after him:
texts.mrk.1.37: and having found him, they say to him, All seek thee.
texts.mrk.1.38: And he says to them, Let us go elsewhere into the neighbouring country towns, that I may preach there also, for for this purpose am I come forth.
texts.mrk.1.39: And he was preaching in their synagogues in the whole of Galilee, and casting out demons.
texts.mrk.1.40: And there comes to him a leper, beseeching him, and falling on his knees to him, and saying to him, If thou wilt thou canst cleanse me.
texts.mrk.1.41: But Jesus, moved with compassion, having stretched out his hand, touched him, and says to him, I will, be thou cleansed.
texts.mrk.1.42: And as he spoke straightway the leprosy left him, and he was cleansed.
texts.mrk.1.43: And having sharply charged him, he straightway sent him away,
texts.mrk.1.44: and says to him, See thou say nothing to any one, but go, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing what Moses ordained, for a testimony to them.
texts.mrk.1.45: But he, having gone forth, began to proclaim [it] much, and to spread the matter abroad, so that he could no longer enter openly into the city, but was without in desert places, and they came to him from every side.
texts.mrk.2.1: And he entered again into Capernaum after [several] days, and it was reported that he was at [the] house;
texts.mrk.2.2: and straightway many were gathered together, so that there was no longer any room, not even at the door; and he spoke the word to them.
texts.mrk.2.3: And there come to him [men] bringing a paralytic, borne by four;
texts.mrk.2.4: and, not being able to get near to him on account of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was, and having dug [it] up they let down the couch on which the paralytic lay.
texts.mrk.2.5: But Jesus, seeing their faith, says to the paralytic, Child, thy sins are forgiven [thee].
texts.mrk.2.6: But certain of the scribes were there sitting, and reasoning in their hearts,
texts.mrk.2.7: Why does this [man] thus speak? he blasphemes. Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?
texts.mrk.2.8: And straightway Jesus, knowing in his spirit that they are reasoning thus within themselves, said to them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?
texts.mrk.2.9: Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, [Thy] sins are forgiven [thee]; or to say, Arise, and take up thy couch and walk?
texts.mrk.2.10: But that ye may know that the Son of man has power on earth to forgive sins, he says to the paralytic,
texts.mrk.2.11: To thee I say, Arise, take up thy couch and go to thine house.
texts.mrk.2.12: And he rose up straightway, and, having taken up his couch, went out before [them] all, so that all were amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it thus.
texts.mrk.2.13: And he went out again by the sea, and all the crowd came to him, and he taught them.
texts.mrk.2.14: And passing by, he saw Levi the [son] of Alphaeus sitting at the tax-office, and says to him, Follow me. And he rose up and followed him.
texts.mrk.2.15: And it came to pass as he lay at table in his house, that many tax-gatherers and sinners lay at table with Jesus and his disciples; for they were many, and they followed him.
texts.mrk.2.16: And the scribes and the Pharisees, seeing him eating with sinners and tax-gatherers, said to his disciples, Why [is it] that he eats and drinks with tax-gatherers and sinners?
texts.mrk.2.17: And Jesus having heard [it] says to them, They that are strong have not need of a physician, but those who are ill. I have not come to call righteous [men], but sinners.
texts.mrk.2.18: And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting; and they come and say to him, Why do the disciples of John and [the disciples] of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?
texts.mrk.2.19: And Jesus said to them, Can the sons of the bride-chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them they cannot fast.
texts.mrk.2.20: But days will come when the bridegroom shall have been taken away from them, and then shall they fast in that day.
texts.mrk.2.21: No one sews a patch of new cloth on an old garment: otherwise its new filling-up takes from the old [stuff], and there is a worse rent.
texts.mrk.2.22: And no one puts new wine into old skins; otherwise the wine bursts the skins, and the wine is poured out, and the skins will be destroyed; but new wine is to be put into new skins.
texts.mrk.2.23: And it came to pass that he went on the sabbath through the cornfields; and his disciples began to walk on, plucking the ears.
texts.mrk.2.24: And the Pharisees said to him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath what is not lawful?
texts.mrk.2.25: And *he* said to them, Have ye never read what David did when he had need and hungered, *he* and those with him,
texts.mrk.2.26: how he entered into the house of God, in [the section of] Abiathar [the] high priest, and ate the shew-bread, which it is not lawful unless for the priests to eat, and gave even to those that were with him?
texts.mrk.2.27: And he said to them, The sabbath was made on account of man, not man on account of the sabbath;
texts.mrk.2.28: so that the Son of man is lord of the sabbath also.
texts.mrk.3.1: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was there a man having his hand dried up.
texts.mrk.3.2: And they watched him if he would heal him on the sabbath, that they might accuse him.
texts.mrk.3.3: And he says to the man who had his hand dried up, Rise up [and come] into the midst.
texts.mrk.3.4: And he says to them, Is it lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to kill? But they were silent.
texts.mrk.3.5: And looking round upon them with anger, distressed at the hardening of their heart, he says to the man, Stretch out thy hand. And he stretched [it] out, and his hand was restored.
texts.mrk.3.6: And the Pharisees going out straightway with the Herodians took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
texts.mrk.3.7: And Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea; and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,
texts.mrk.3.8: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea and beyond the Jordan; and they of around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, having heard what things he did, came to him.
texts.mrk.3.9: And he spoke to his disciples, in order that a little ship should wait upon him on account of the crowd, that they might not press upon him.
texts.mrk.3.10: For he healed many, so that they beset him that they might touch him, as many as had plagues.
texts.mrk.3.11: And the unclean spirits, when they beheld him, fell down before him, and cried saying, *Thou* art the Son of God.
texts.mrk.3.12: And he rebuked them much, that they might not make him manifest.
texts.mrk.3.13: And he goes up into the mountain, and calls whom he himself would, and they went to him.
texts.mrk.3.14: And he appointed twelve that they might be with him, and that he might send them to preach,
texts.mrk.3.15: and to have power [to heal diseases, and] to cast out demons.
texts.mrk.3.16: And he gave to Simon the surname of Peter;
texts.mrk.3.17: and James the [son] of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and he gave them the surname of Boanerges, that is, Sons of thunder;
texts.mrk.3.18: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the [son] of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Cananaean,
texts.mrk.3.19: and Judas Iscariote, who also delivered him up. And they come to [the] house.
texts.mrk.3.20: And again a crowd comes together, so that they cannot even eat bread.
texts.mrk.3.21: And his relatives having heard [of it] went out to lay hold on him, for they said, He is out of his mind.
texts.mrk.3.22: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said, He has Beelzebub, and, By the prince of the demons he casts out demons.
texts.mrk.3.23: And having called them to [him], he said to them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?
texts.mrk.3.24: And if a kingdom has become divided against itself, that kingdom cannot subsist.
texts.mrk.3.25: And if a house has become divided against itself, that house cannot subsist.
texts.mrk.3.26: And if Satan rise up against himself, and is divided, he cannot subsist, but has an end.
texts.mrk.3.27: But no one can, having entered into his house, plunder the goods of the strong [man] unless he first bind the strong [man], and then he will plunder his house.
texts.mrk.3.28: Verily I say unto you, that all sins shall be forgiven to the sons of men, and all the injurious speeches [with] which they may speak injuriously;
texts.mrk.3.29: but whosoever shall speak injuriously against the Holy Spirit, to eternity has no forgiveness; but lies under the guilt of an everlasting sin;
texts.mrk.3.30: -- because they said, He has an unclean spirit.
texts.mrk.3.31: And his brethren and his mother come, and standing without sent to him calling him.
texts.mrk.3.32: And a crowd sat around him. And they said to him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren seek thee without.
texts.mrk.3.33: And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother or my brethren?
texts.mrk.3.34: And looking around in a circuit at those that were sitting around him, he says, Behold my mother and my brethren:
texts.mrk.3.35: for whosoever shall do the will of God, *he* is my brother, and sister, and mother.
texts.mrk.4.1: And again he began to teach by the sea. And a great crowd was gathered together to him, so that going on board ship he sat in the sea, and all the crowd were close to the sea on the land.
texts.mrk.4.2: And he taught them many things in parables. And he said to them in his doctrine,
texts.mrk.4.3: Hearken: Behold, the sower went forth to sow.
texts.mrk.4.4: And it came to pass as he sowed, one fell by the wayside, and the birds came and devoured it.
texts.mrk.4.5: And another fell on the rocky ground, where it had not much earth, and immediately it sprung up out [of the ground] because it had no depth of earth;
texts.mrk.4.6: and when the sun arose it was burnt up, and because of its not having any root, it withered.
texts.mrk.4.7: And another fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
texts.mrk.4.8: And another fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing; and bore, one thirty, and one sixty, and one a hundred.
texts.mrk.4.9: And he said, He that has ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mrk.4.10: And when he was alone, those about him with the twelve asked him [as to] the parables.
texts.mrk.4.11: And he said to them, To you is given [to know] the mystery of the kingdom of God; but to them who are without, all things are done in parables,
texts.mrk.4.12: that beholding they may behold and not see, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest it may be, they should be converted and they should be forgiven.
texts.mrk.4.13: And he says to them, Do ye not know this parable? and how will ye be acquainted with all the parables?
texts.mrk.4.15: and these are they by the wayside where the word is sown, and when they hear, immediately Satan comes and takes away the word that was sown in them.
texts.mrk.4.16: And these are they in like manner who are sown upon the rocky places, who when they hear the word, immediately receive it with joy,
texts.mrk.4.17: and they have no root in themselves, but are for a time: then, tribulation arising, or persecution on account of the word, immediately they are offended.
texts.mrk.4.18: And others are they who are sown among the thorns: these are they who have heard the word,
texts.mrk.4.19: and the cares of life, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things, entering in, choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
texts.mrk.4.20: And these are they who have been sown on the good ground, such as hear the word and receive it, and bear fruit; one thirty, and one sixty, and one a hundred [fold].
texts.mrk.4.21: And he said to them, Does the lamp come that it should be put under the bushel or under the couch? [Is it] not that it should be set upon the lamp-stand?
texts.mrk.4.22: For there is nothing hidden which shall not be made manifest; nor does any secret thing take place, but that it should come to light.
texts.mrk.4.23: If any one have ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mrk.4.24: And he said to them, Take heed what ye hear; with what measure ye mete, it shall be meted to you; and there shall be [more] added to you.
texts.mrk.4.25: For whosoever has, to him shall be given; and he who has not, even what he has shall be taken from him.
texts.mrk.4.26: And he said, Thus is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast the seed upon the earth,
texts.mrk.4.27: and should sleep and rise up night and day, and the seed should sprout and grow, he does not know how.
texts.mrk.4.28: The earth bears fruit of itself, first [the] blade, then an ear, then full corn in the ear.
texts.mrk.4.29: But when the fruit is produced, immediately he sends the sickle, for the harvest is come.
texts.mrk.4.30: And he said, How should we liken the kingdom of God, or with what comparison should we compare it?
texts.mrk.4.31: As to a grain of mustard [seed], which, when it is sown upon the earth, is less than all seeds which are upon the earth,
texts.mrk.4.32: and when it has been sown, mounts up and becomes greater than all herbs, and produces great branches, so that the birds of heaven can roost under its shadow.
texts.mrk.4.33: And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear,
texts.mrk.4.34: but without a parable spoke he not to them; and in private he explained all things to his disciples.
texts.mrk.4.35: And on that day, when evening was come, he says to them, Let us go over to the other side:
texts.mrk.4.36: and having sent away the crowd, they take him with [them], as he was, in the ship. But other ships also were with him.
texts.mrk.4.37: And there comes a violent gust of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it already filled.
texts.mrk.4.38: And *he* was in the stern sleeping on the cushion. And they awake him up and say to him, Teacher, dost thou not care that we are perishing?
texts.mrk.4.39: And awaking up he rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, Silence; be mute. And the wind fell, and there was a great calm.
texts.mrk.4.40: And he said to them, Why are ye [thus] fearful? how [is it] ye have not faith?
texts.mrk.4.41: And they feared [with] great fear, and said one to another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
texts.mrk.5.1: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gadarenes.
texts.mrk.5.2: And immediately on his going out of the ship there met him out of the tombs a man possessed by an unclean spirit,
texts.mrk.5.3: who had his dwelling in the tombs; and no one was able to bind him, not even with chains;
texts.mrk.5.4: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn asunder by him, and the fetters were shattered; and no one was able to subdue him.
texts.mrk.5.5: And continually night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying and cutting himself with stones.
texts.mrk.5.6: But seeing Jesus from afar off, he ran and did him homage,
texts.mrk.5.7: and crying with a loud voice he says, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I adjure thee by God, torment me not.
texts.mrk.5.8: For he said to him, Come forth, unclean spirit, out of the man.
texts.mrk.5.9: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he says to him, Legion is my name, because we are many.
texts.mrk.5.10: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
texts.mrk.5.11: Now there was there just at the mountain a great herd of swine feeding;
texts.mrk.5.12: and they besought him, saying, Send us into the swine that we may enter into them.
texts.mrk.5.13: And Jesus [immediately] allowed them. And the unclean spirits going out entered into the swine, and the herd rushed down the steep slope, into the sea (about two thousand), and were choked in the sea.
texts.mrk.5.14: And those that were feeding them fled and reported it in the city and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that had taken place.
texts.mrk.5.15: And they come to Jesus, and they see the possessed of demons sitting [and] clothed and sensible, [him] that had had the legion: and they were afraid.
texts.mrk.5.16: And they that had seen [it] related to them how it had happened to the [man] possessed by demons, and concerning the swine.
texts.mrk.5.17: And they began to beg him to depart from their coasts.
texts.mrk.5.18: And as he went on board ship, the man that had been possessed by demons besought him that he might be with him.
texts.mrk.5.19: And he suffered him not, but says to him, Go to thine home to thine own people, and tell them how great things the Lord has done for thee, and has had mercy on thee.
texts.mrk.5.20: And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him; and all wondered.
texts.mrk.5.21: And Jesus having passed over in the ship again to the other side, a great crowd gathered to him; and he was by the sea.
texts.mrk.5.22: And [behold] there comes one of the rulers of the synagogue, by name Jairus, and seeing him, falls down at his feet;
texts.mrk.5.23: and he besought him much, saying, My little daughter is at extremity; [I pray] that thou shouldest come and lay thy hands upon her so that she may be healed, and may live.
texts.mrk.5.24: And he went with him, and a large crowd followed him and pressed on him.
texts.mrk.5.25: And a certain woman who had had a flux of blood twelve years,
texts.mrk.5.26: and had suffered much under many physicians, and had spent everything she had and had found no advantage from it, but had rather got worse,
texts.mrk.5.27: having heard concerning Jesus, came in the crowd behind and touched his clothes;
texts.mrk.5.28: for she said, If I shall touch but his clothes I shall be healed.
texts.mrk.5.29: And immediately her fountain of blood was dried up, and she knew in her body that she was cured from the scourge.
texts.mrk.5.30: And immediately Jesus, knowing in himself the power that had gone out of him, turning round in the crowd said, Who has touched my clothes?
texts.mrk.5.31: And his disciples said to him, Thou seest the crowd pressing on thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
texts.mrk.5.32: And he looked round about to see her who had done this.
texts.mrk.5.33: But the woman, frightened and trembling, knowing what had taken place in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
texts.mrk.5.34: And he said to her, Daughter, thy faith has healed thee; go in peace, and be well of thy scourge.
texts.mrk.5.35: While he was yet speaking, they come from the ruler of the synagogue's [house], saying, Thy daughter has died, why troublest thou the teacher any further?
texts.mrk.5.36: But Jesus [immediately], having heard the word spoken, says to the ruler of the synagogue, Fear not; only believe.
texts.mrk.5.37: And he suffered no one to accompany him save Peter and James, and John the brother of James.
texts.mrk.5.38: And he comes to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and sees the tumult, and people weeping and wailing greatly.
texts.mrk.5.39: And entering in he says to them, Why do ye make a tumult and weep? the child has not died, but sleeps.
texts.mrk.5.40: And they derided him. But he, having put [them] all out, takes with [him] the father of the child, and the mother, and those that were with him, and enters in where the child was lying.
texts.mrk.5.41: And having laid hold of the hand of the child, he says to her, Talitha koumi, which is, interpreted, Damsel, I say to thee, Arise.
texts.mrk.5.42: And immediately the damsel arose and walked, for she was twelve years old. And they were astonished with great astonishment.
texts.mrk.5.43: And he charged them much that no one should know this; and he desired that [something] should be given her to eat.
texts.mrk.6.1: And he went out thence and came to his own country, and his disciples follow him.
texts.mrk.6.2: And when sabbath was come he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing were amazed, saying, Whence [has] this [man] these things? and what [is] the wisdom that is given to him, and such works of power are done by his hands?
texts.mrk.6.3: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, and Joses, and Judas, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended in him.
texts.mrk.6.4: But Jesus said to them, A prophet is not despised save in his own country, and among [his] kinsmen, and in his own house.
texts.mrk.6.5: And he could not do any work of power there, save that laying his hands on a few infirm persons he healed [them].
texts.mrk.6.6: And he wondered because of their unbelief. And he went round the villages in a circuit, teaching.
texts.mrk.6.7: And he calls the twelve to [him]; and he began to send them out two [and] two, and gave to them power over the unclean spirits;
texts.mrk.6.8: and he commanded them that they should take nothing for the way, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their belt;
texts.mrk.6.9: but be shod with sandals, and put not on two body-coats.
texts.mrk.6.10: And he said to them, Wheresoever ye shall enter into a house, there remain till ye shall go thence.
texts.mrk.6.11: And whatsoever place shall not receive you nor hear you, departing thence, shake off the dust which is under your feet for a testimony to them.
texts.mrk.6.12: And they went forth and preached that they should repent;
texts.mrk.6.13: and they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many infirm, and healed them.
texts.mrk.6.14: And Herod the king heard [of him] (for his name had become public), and said, John the baptist is risen from among [the] dead, and on this account works of power are wrought by him.
texts.mrk.6.15: And others said, It is Elias; and others said, It is a prophet, as one of the prophets.
texts.mrk.6.16: But Herod when he heard [it] said, John whom *I* beheaded, he it is; *he* is risen [from among the dead].
texts.mrk.6.17: For the same Herod had sent and seized John, and had bound him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, because he had married her.
texts.mrk.6.18: For John said to Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have the wife of thy brother.
texts.mrk.6.19: But Herodias kept it [in her mind] against him, and wished to kill him, and could not:
texts.mrk.6.20: for Herod feared John knowing that he was a just and holy man, and kept him safe; and having heard him, did many things, and heard him gladly.
texts.mrk.6.21: And a holiday being come, when Herod, on his birthday, made a supper to his grandees, and to the chiliarchs, and the chief [men] of Galilee;
texts.mrk.6.22: and the daughter of the same Herodias having come in, and danced, pleased Herod and those that were with [him] at table; and the king said to the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt and I will give it thee.
texts.mrk.6.23: And he swore to her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask me I will give thee, to half of my kingdom.
texts.mrk.6.24: And she went out, and said to her mother, What should I ask? And she said, The head of John the baptist.
texts.mrk.6.25: And immediately going in with haste to the king, she asked saying, I desire that thou give me directly upon a dish the head of John the baptist.
texts.mrk.6.26: And the king, [while] made very sorry, on account of the oaths and those lying at table with [him] would not break his word with her.
texts.mrk.6.27: And immediately the king, having sent one of the guard, ordered his head to be brought. And he went out and beheaded him in the prison,
texts.mrk.6.28: and brought his head upon a dish, and gave it to the damsel, and the damsel gave it to her mother.
texts.mrk.6.29: And his disciples having heard [it], came and took up his body, and laid it in a tomb.
texts.mrk.6.30: And the apostles are gathered together to Jesus. And they related to him all things, [both] what they had done and what they had taught.
texts.mrk.6.31: And he said to them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place and rest a little. For those coming and those going were many, and they had not leisure even to eat.
texts.mrk.6.32: And they went away apart into a desert place by ship.
texts.mrk.6.33: And many saw them going, and recognised them, and ran together there on foot, out of all the cities, and got [there] before them.
texts.mrk.6.34: And on leaving [the ship] [Jesus] saw a great crowd, and he was moved with compassion for them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd. And he began to teach them many things.
texts.mrk.6.35: And when it was already late in the day, his disciples coming to him say, The place is desert, and it is already late in the day;
texts.mrk.6.36: send them away that they may go into the country and villages around, and buy themselves bread, for they have not anything they can eat.
texts.mrk.6.37: And he answering said to them, Give *ye* them to eat. And they say to him, Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread and give them to eat?
texts.mrk.6.38: And he says to them, How many loaves have ye? Go [and] see. And when they knew they say, Five, and two fishes.
texts.mrk.6.39: And he ordered them to make them all sit down by companies on the green grass.
texts.mrk.6.40: And they sat down in ranks by hundreds and by fifties.
texts.mrk.6.41: And having taken the five loaves and the two fishes, looking up to heaven, he blessed, and broke the loaves, and gave [them] to his disciples that they might set [them] before them. And the two fishes he divided among all.
texts.mrk.6.42: And they all ate and were satisfied.
texts.mrk.6.43: And they took up of fragments the fillings of twelve hand-baskets, and of the fishes.
texts.mrk.6.44: And those that ate of the loaves were five thousand men.
texts.mrk.6.45: And immediately he compelled his disciples to go on board ship, and to go on before to the other side to Bethsaida, while *he* sends the crowd away.
texts.mrk.6.46: And, having dismissed them, he departed into the mountain to pray.
texts.mrk.6.47: And when evening was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and *he* alone upon the land.
texts.mrk.6.48: And seeing them labouring in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he comes to them walking on the sea, and would have passed them by.
texts.mrk.6.49: But they, seeing him walking on the sea, thought that it was an apparition, and cried out.
texts.mrk.6.50: For all saw him and were troubled. And immediately he spoke with them, and says to them, Be of good courage: it is *I*; be not afraid.
texts.mrk.6.51: And he went up to them into the ship, and the wind fell. And they were exceedingly beyond measure astonished in themselves and wondered;
texts.mrk.6.52: for they understood not through the loaves: for their heart was hardened.
texts.mrk.6.53: And having passed over, they came to the land of Gennesaret and made the shore.
texts.mrk.6.54: And on their coming out of the ship, immediately recognising him,
texts.mrk.6.55: they ran through that whole country around, and began to carry about those that were ill on couches, where they heard that he was.
texts.mrk.6.56: And wherever he entered into villages, or cities, or the country, they laid the sick in the market-places, and besought him that they might touch if it were only the hem of his garment; and as many as touched him were healed.
texts.mrk.7.1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, coming from Jerusalem, are gathered together to him,
texts.mrk.7.2: and seeing some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is, unwashed, hands,
texts.mrk.7.3: (for the Pharisees and all the Jews, unless they wash their hands diligently, do not eat, holding what has been delivered by the ancients;
texts.mrk.7.4: and [on coming] from the market-place, unless they are washed, they do not eat; and there are many other things which they have received to hold, the washing of cups and vessels, and brazen utensils, and couches),
texts.mrk.7.5: then the Pharisees and the scribes ask him, Why do thy disciples not walk according to what has been delivered by the ancients, but eat the bread with defiled hands?
texts.mrk.7.6: But he answering said to them, Well did Esaias prophesy concerning you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honour me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me.
texts.mrk.7.7: But in vain do they worship me, teaching [as their] teachings commandments of men.
texts.mrk.7.8: [For], leaving the commandment of God, ye hold what is delivered by men [to keep] -- washings of vessels and cups, and many other such like things ye do.
texts.mrk.7.9: And he said to them, Well do ye set aside the commandment of God, that ye may observe what is delivered by yourselves [to keep].
texts.mrk.7.10: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, he who speaks ill of father or mother, let him surely die.
texts.mrk.7.11: But *ye* say, If a man say to his father or his mother, [It is] corban (that is, gift), whatsoever thou mightest have profit from me by ...
texts.mrk.7.12: And ye no longer suffer him to do anything for his father or his mother;
texts.mrk.7.13: making void the word of God by your traditional teaching which ye have delivered; and many such like things ye do.
texts.mrk.7.14: And having called again the crowd, he said to them, Hear me, all [of you], and understand:
texts.mrk.7.15: There is nothing from outside a man entering into him which can defile him; but the things which go out from him, those it is which defile the man.
texts.mrk.7.16: If any one have ears to hear, let him hear.
texts.mrk.7.17: And when he went indoors from the crowd, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
texts.mrk.7.18: And he says to them, Are *ye* also thus unintelligent? Do ye not perceive that all that is outside entering into the man cannot defile him,
texts.mrk.7.19: because it does not enter into his heart but into his belly, and goes out into the draught, purging all meats?
texts.mrk.7.20: And he said, That which goes forth out of the man, that defiles the man.
texts.mrk.7.21: For from within, out of the heart of men, go forth evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
texts.mrk.7.22: thefts, covetousness, wickednesses, deceit, licentiousness, a wicked eye, injurious language, haughtiness, folly;
texts.mrk.7.23: all these wicked things go forth from within and defile the man.
texts.mrk.7.24: And he rose up and went away thence into the borders of Tyre and Sidon; and having entered into a house he would not have any one know [it], and he could not be hid.
texts.mrk.7.25: But immediately a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell at his feet
texts.mrk.7.26: (and the woman was a Greek, Syrophenician by race), and asked him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
texts.mrk.7.27: But [Jesus] said to her, Suffer the children to be first filled; for it is not right to take the children's bread and cast it to the dogs.
texts.mrk.7.28: But she answered and says to him, Yea, Lord; for even the dogs under the table eat of the children's crumbs.
texts.mrk.7.29: And he said to her, Because of this word, go thy way, the demon is gone out of thy daughter.
texts.mrk.7.30: And having gone away to her house she found the demon gone out, and her daughter lying on the bed.
texts.mrk.7.31: And again having left the borders of Tyre and Sidon, he came to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
texts.mrk.7.32: And they bring to him a deaf [man] who could not speak right, and they beseech him that he might lay his hand on him.
texts.mrk.7.33: And having taken him away from the crowd apart, he put his fingers to his ears; and having spit, he touched his tongue;
texts.mrk.7.34: and looking up to heaven he groaned, and says to him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
texts.mrk.7.35: And immediately his ears were opened, and the band of his tongue was loosed and he spoke right.
texts.mrk.7.36: And he charged them that they should speak to no one [of it]. But so much the more *he* charged them, so much the more abundantly *they* proclaimed it;
texts.mrk.7.37: and they were astonished above measure, saying, He does all things well; he makes both the deaf to hear, and the speechless to speak.
texts.mrk.8.1: In those days, there being again a great crowd, and they having nothing that they could eat, having called his disciples to [him], he says to them,
texts.mrk.8.2: I have compassion on the crowd, because they have stayed with me already three days and they have not anything they can eat,
texts.mrk.8.3: and if I should dismiss them to their home fasting, they will faint on the way; for some of them are come from far.
texts.mrk.8.4: And his disciples answered him, Whence shall one be able to satisfy these with bread here in a desert place?
texts.mrk.8.5: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.
texts.mrk.8.6: And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground. And having taken the seven loaves, he gave thanks, and broke [them] and gave [them] to his disciples, that they might set [them] before [them]; and they set [them] before the crowd.
texts.mrk.8.7: And they had a few small fishes, and having blessed them, he desired these also to be set before [them].
texts.mrk.8.8: And they ate and were satisfied. And they took up of fragments that remained seven baskets.
texts.mrk.8.9: And they [that had eaten] were about four thousand; and he sent them away.
texts.mrk.8.10: And immediately going on board ship with his disciples, he came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
texts.mrk.8.11: And the Pharisees went out and began to dispute against him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, tempting him.
texts.mrk.8.12: And groaning in his spirit, he says, Why does this generation seek a sign? Verily I say unto you, A sign shall in no wise be given to this generation.
texts.mrk.8.13: And he left them, and going again on board ship, went away to the other side.
texts.mrk.8.14: And they forgot to take bread, and save one loaf, they had not [any] with them in the ship.
texts.mrk.8.15: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and [of] the leaven of Herod.
texts.mrk.8.16: And they reasoned with one another, [saying], It is because we have no bread.
texts.mrk.8.17: And Jesus knowing [it], says to them, Why reason ye because ye have no bread? Do ye not yet perceive nor understand? Have ye your heart [yet] hardened?
texts.mrk.8.18: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
texts.mrk.8.19: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many hand-baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say to him, Twelve.
texts.mrk.8.20: And when the seven for the four thousand, the filling of how many baskets of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.
texts.mrk.8.21: And he said to them, How do ye not yet understand?
texts.mrk.8.22: And he comes to Bethsaida; and they bring him a blind man, and beseech him that he might touch him.
