texts.mrk.8.23: And taking hold of the hand of the blind man he led him forth out of the village, and having spit upon his eyes, he laid his hands upon him, and asked him if he beheld anything.
texts.mrk.8.24: And having looked up, he said, I behold men, for I see [them], as trees, walking.
texts.mrk.8.25: Then he laid his hands again upon his eyes, and he saw distinctly, and was restored and saw all things clearly.
texts.mrk.8.26: And he sent him to his house, saying, Neither enter into the village, nor tell [it] to any one in the village.
texts.mrk.8.27: And Jesus went forth and his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea-Philippi. And by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Who do men say that I am?
texts.mrk.8.28: And they answered him, saying, John the baptist; and others, Elias; but others, One of the prophets.
texts.mrk.8.29: And he asked them, But *ye*, who do ye say that I am? And Peter answering says to him, *Thou* art the Christ.
texts.mrk.8.30: And he charged them straitly, in order that they should tell no man about him.
texts.mrk.8.31: And he began to teach them that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders and of the chief priests and of the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise [again].
texts.mrk.8.32: And he spoke the thing openly. And Peter, taking him to [him], began to rebuke him.
texts.mrk.8.33: But he, turning round and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, saying, Get away behind me, Satan, for thy mind is not on the things that are of God, but on the things that are of men.
texts.mrk.8.34: And having called the crowd with his disciples, he said to them, Whoever desires to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross and follow me.
texts.mrk.8.35: For whosoever shall desire to save his life shall lose it, but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel's shall save it.
texts.mrk.8.36: For what shall it profit a man if he gain the whole world and suffer the loss of his soul?
texts.mrk.8.37: for what should a man give in exchange for his soul?
texts.mrk.8.38: For whosoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, of him shall the Son of man also be ashamed when he shall come in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
texts.mrk.9.1: And he said to them, Verily I say unto you, There are some of those standing here that shall not taste death until they shall have seen the kingdom of God come in power.
texts.mrk.9.2: And after six days Jesus takes with [him] Peter and James and John, and takes them up on a high mountain by themselves apart. And he was transfigured before them:
texts.mrk.9.3: and his garments became shining, exceeding white [as snow], such as fuller on earth could not whiten [them].
texts.mrk.9.4: And there appeared to them Elias with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
texts.mrk.9.5: And Peter answering says to Jesus, Rabbi, it is good that we should be here; and let us make three tabernacles, for thee one, and for Moses one, and for Elias one.
texts.mrk.9.6: For he knew not what he should say, for they were filled with fear.
texts.mrk.9.7: And there came a cloud overshadowing them, and there came a voice out of the cloud, *This* is my beloved Son: hear him.
texts.mrk.9.8: And suddenly having looked around, they no longer saw any one, but Jesus alone with themselves.
texts.mrk.9.9: And as they descended from the mountain, he charged them that they should relate to no one what they had seen, unless when the Son of man should be risen from among [the] dead.
texts.mrk.9.10: And they kept that saying, questioning among themselves, what rising from among [the] dead was.
texts.mrk.9.11: And they asked him saying, Why do the scribes say that Elias must first have come?
texts.mrk.9.12: And he answering said to them, Elias indeed, having first come, restores all things; and how is it written of the Son of man that he must suffer much, and be set at nought:
texts.mrk.9.13: but I say unto you that Elias also is come, and they have done to him whatever they would, as it is written of him.
texts.mrk.9.14: And when he came to the disciples he saw a great crowd around them, and scribes disputing against them.
texts.mrk.9.15: And immediately all the crowd seeing him were amazed, and running to [him], saluted him.
texts.mrk.9.16: And he asked them, What do ye question with them about?
texts.mrk.9.17: And one out of the crowd answered him, Teacher, I brought to thee my son, who has a dumb spirit;
texts.mrk.9.18: and wheresoever it seizes him it tears him, and he foams and gnashes his teeth, and he is withering away. And I spoke to thy disciples, that they might cast him out, and they could not.
texts.mrk.9.19: But he answering them says, O unbelieving generation! how long shall I be with you? how long shall I bear with you? bring him to me.
texts.mrk.9.20: And they brought him to him. And seeing him the spirit immediately tore him; and falling upon the earth he rolled foaming.
texts.mrk.9.21: And he asked his father, How long a time is it that it has been like this with him? And he said, From childhood;
texts.mrk.9.22: and often it has cast him both into fire and into waters that it might destroy him: but if thou couldst [do] anything, be moved with pity on us, and help us.
texts.mrk.9.23: And Jesus said to him, The 'if thou couldst' is [if thou couldst] believe: all things are possible to him that believes.
texts.mrk.9.24: And immediately the father of the young child crying out said [with tears], I believe, help mine unbelief.
texts.mrk.9.25: But Jesus, seeing that [the] crowd was running up together, rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, *I* command thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
texts.mrk.9.26: And having cried out and torn [him] much, he came out; and he became as if dead, so that the most said, He is dead.
texts.mrk.9.27: But Jesus, having taken hold of him by the hand, lifted him up, and he arose.
texts.mrk.9.28: And when he was entered into the house, his disciples asked him privately, Wherefore could not *we* cast him out?
texts.mrk.9.29: And he said to them, This kind can go out by nothing but by prayer and fasting.
texts.mrk.9.30: And going forth from thence they went through Galilee; and he would not that any one knew it;
texts.mrk.9.31: for he taught his disciples and said to them, The Son of man is delivered into men's hands, and they shall kill him; and having been killed, after three days he shall rise again.
texts.mrk.9.32: But they understood not the saying, and feared to ask him.
texts.mrk.9.33: And he came to Capernaum, and being in the house, he asked them, Of what were ye reasoning by the way?
texts.mrk.9.34: And they remained silent, for by the way they had been reasoning with one another who [was] greatest.
texts.mrk.9.35: And sitting down he called the twelve; and he says to them, If any one would be first, he shall be last of all, and minister of all.
texts.mrk.9.36: And taking a little child he set it in their midst, and having taken it in his arms he said to them,
texts.mrk.9.37: Whosoever shall receive one of such little children in my name, receives me; and whosoever shall receive me, does not receive me, but him who sent me.
texts.mrk.9.38: And John answered him saying, Teacher, we saw some one casting out demons in thy name, who does not follow us, and we forbad him, because he does not follow us.
texts.mrk.9.39: But Jesus said, Forbid him not; for there is no one who shall do a miracle in my name, and be able soon [after] to speak ill of me;
texts.mrk.9.40: for he who is not against us is for us.
texts.mrk.9.41: For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink in [my] name, because ye are Christ's, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
texts.mrk.9.42: And whosoever shall be a snare to one of the little ones who believe [in me], it were better for him if a millstone were hung about his neck, and he cast into the sea.
texts.mrk.9.43: And if thy hand serve as a snare to thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having thy two hands to go away into hell, into the fire unquenchable;
texts.mrk.9.44: [where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched].
texts.mrk.9.45: And if thy foot serve as a snare to thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life lame, than having thy two feet to be cast into hell, into the fire unquenchable;
texts.mrk.9.46: [where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched].
texts.mrk.9.47: And if thine eye serve as a snare to thee, cast it out: it is better for thee to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into the hell of fire,
texts.mrk.9.48: where their worm dies not, and the fire is not quenched.
texts.mrk.9.49: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt.
texts.mrk.9.50: Salt [is] good, but if the salt is become saltless, wherewith will ye season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.
texts.mrk.10.1: And rising up thence he comes into the coasts of Judaea, and the other side of the Jordan. And again crowds come together to him, and, as he was accustomed, again he taught them.
texts.mrk.10.2: And Pharisees coming to [him] asked him, Is it lawful for a man to put away [his] wife? (tempting him).
texts.mrk.10.3: But he answering said to them, What did Moses command you?
texts.mrk.10.4: And they said, Moses allowed to write a bill of divorce, and to put away.
texts.mrk.10.5: And Jesus answering said to them, In view of your hard-heartedness he wrote this commandment for you;
texts.mrk.10.6: but from [the] beginning of [the] creation God made them male and female.
texts.mrk.10.7: For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother and shall be united to his wife,
texts.mrk.10.8: and the two shall be one flesh: so that they are no longer two but one flesh.
texts.mrk.10.9: What therefore God has joined together, let not man separate.
texts.mrk.10.10: And again in the house the disciples asked him concerning this.
texts.mrk.10.11: And he says to them, Whosoever shall put away his wife and shall marry another, commits adultery against her.
texts.mrk.10.12: And if a woman put away her husband and shall marry another, she commits adultery.
texts.mrk.10.13: And they brought little children to him that he might touch them. But the disciples rebuked those that brought [them].
texts.mrk.10.14: But Jesus seeing [it], was indignant, and said to them, Suffer the little children to come to me; forbid them not; for of such is the kingdom of God.
texts.mrk.10.15: Verily I say to you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, shall in no wise enter into it.
texts.mrk.10.16: And having taken them in his arms, having laid his hands on them, he blessed them.
texts.mrk.10.17: And as he went forth into the way, a person ran up to [him], and kneeling to him asked him, Good Teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
texts.mrk.10.18: But Jesus said to him, Why callest thou me good? no one is good but one, [that is] God.
texts.mrk.10.19: Thou knowest the commandments: Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Do not defraud, Honour thy father and mother.
texts.mrk.10.20: And he answering said to him, Teacher, all these things have I kept from my youth.
texts.mrk.10.21: And Jesus looking upon him loved him, and said to him, One thing lackest thou: go, sell whatever thou hast and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, [taking up the cross].
texts.mrk.10.22: But he, sad at the word, went away grieved, for he had large possessions.
texts.mrk.10.23: And Jesus looking around says to his disciples, How difficultly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!
texts.mrk.10.24: And the disciples were amazed at his words. And Jesus again answering says to them, Children, how difficult it is that those who trust in riches should enter into the kingdom of God!
texts.mrk.10.25: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
texts.mrk.10.26: And they were exceedingly astonished, saying to one another, And who can be saved?
texts.mrk.10.27: But Jesus looking on them says, With men it is impossible, but not with God; for all things are possible with God.
texts.mrk.10.28: Peter began to say to him, Behold, *we* have left all things and have followed thee.
texts.mrk.10.29: Jesus answering said, Verily I say to you, There is no one who has left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, [or wife], or children, or lands, for my sake and for the sake of the gospel,
texts.mrk.10.30: that shall not receive a hundredfold now in this time: houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions, and in the coming age life eternal.
texts.mrk.10.31: But many first shall be last, and the last first.
texts.mrk.10.32: And they were in the way going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was going on before them; and they were amazed, and were afraid as they followed. And taking the twelve again to [him], he began to tell them what was going to happen to him:
texts.mrk.10.33: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and the Son of man shall be delivered up to the chief priests and to the scribes, and they shall condemn him to death, and shall deliver him up to the nations:
texts.mrk.10.34: and they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him; and after three days he shall rise again.
texts.mrk.10.35: And there come to him James and John, the sons of Zebedee, saying [to him], Teacher, we would that whatsoever we may ask thee, thou wouldst do it for us.
texts.mrk.10.36: And he said to them, What would ye that I should do for you?
texts.mrk.10.37: And they said to him, Give to us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and one on thy left hand, in thy glory.
texts.mrk.10.38: And Jesus said to them, Ye do not know what ye ask. Are ye able to drink the cup which *I* drink, or be baptised with the baptism that *I* am baptised with?
texts.mrk.10.39: And they said to him, We are able. And Jesus said to them, The cup that *I* drink ye will drink and with the baptism that *I* am baptised with ye will be baptised,
texts.mrk.10.40: but to sit on my right hand or on my left is not mine to give, but for those for whom it is prepared.
texts.mrk.10.41: And the ten having heard [of it], began to be indignant about James and John.
texts.mrk.10.42: But Jesus having called them to [him], says to them, Ye know that those who are esteemed to rule over the nations exercise lordship over them; and their great men exercise authority over them;
texts.mrk.10.43: but it is not thus among you; but whosoever would be great among you, shall be your minister;
texts.mrk.10.44: and whosoever would be first of you shall be bondman of all.
texts.mrk.10.45: For also the Son of man did not come to be ministered to, but to minister, and give his life a ransom for many.
texts.mrk.10.46: And they come to Jericho, and as he was going out from Jericho, and his disciples and a large crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, the blind [man], sat by the wayside begging.
texts.mrk.10.47: And having heard that it was Jesus the Nazaraean, he began to cry out and to say, O Son of David, Jesus, have mercy on me.
texts.mrk.10.48: And many rebuked him, that he might be silent; but he cried so much the more, Son of David, have mercy on me.
texts.mrk.10.49: And Jesus, standing still, desired him to be called. And they call the blind [man], saying to him, Be of good courage, rise up, he calls thee.
texts.mrk.10.50: And, throwing away his garment, he started up and came to Jesus.
texts.mrk.10.51: And Jesus answering says to him, What wilt thou that I shall do to thee? And the blind [man] said to him, Rabboni, that I may see.
texts.mrk.10.52: And Jesus said to him, Go, thy faith has healed thee. And he saw immediately, and followed him in the way.
texts.mrk.11.1: And when they draw near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the mount of Olives, he sends two of his disciples,
texts.mrk.11.2: and says to them, Go into the village which is over against you, and immediately on entering into it ye will find a colt tied, upon which no [child] of man has ever sat: loose it and lead it [here].
texts.mrk.11.3: And if any one say to you, Why do ye this? say, The Lord has need of it; and straightway he sends it hither.
texts.mrk.11.4: And they departed, and found a colt bound to the door without at the crossway, and they loose him.
texts.mrk.11.5: And some of those who stood there said to them, What are ye doing, loosing the colt?
texts.mrk.11.6: And they said to them as Jesus had commanded. And they let them [do it].
texts.mrk.11.7: And they led the colt to Jesus, and cast their clothes upon it, and he sat on it;
texts.mrk.11.8: and many strewed their clothes on the way, and others cut down branches from the trees [and went on strewing them on the way].
texts.mrk.11.9: And those going on before and those following cried out, Hosanna! blessed [be] he that comes in [the] Lord's name.
texts.mrk.11.10: Blessed [be] the coming kingdom of our father David. Hosanna in the highest!
texts.mrk.11.11: And he entered into Jerusalem and into the temple; and having looked round on all things, the hour being already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
texts.mrk.11.12: And on the morrow, when they were gone out of Bethany, he hungered.
texts.mrk.11.13: And seeing from afar off a fig-tree which had leaves, he came, if perhaps he might find something on it. And having come up to it he found nothing but leaves, for it was not the time of figs.
texts.mrk.11.14: And answering he said to it, Let no one eat fruit of thee any more for ever. And his disciples heard [it].
texts.mrk.11.15: And they come to Jerusalem, and entering into the temple, he began to cast out those who sold and who bought in the temple, and he overthrew the tables of the moneychangers and the seats of the dove-sellers,
texts.mrk.11.16: and suffered not that any one should carry any package through the temple.
texts.mrk.11.17: And he taught saying to them, Is it not written, My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations? but *ye* have made it a den of robbers.
texts.mrk.11.18: And the chief priests and the scribes heard [it], and they sought how they might destroy him; for they feared him, because all the crowd were astonished at his doctrine.
texts.mrk.11.19: And when it was evening he went forth without the city.
texts.mrk.11.20: And passing by early in the morning they saw the fig-tree dried up from the roots.
texts.mrk.11.21: And Peter, remembering [what Jesus had said], says to him, Rabbi, see, the fig-tree which thou cursedst is dried up.
texts.mrk.11.22: And Jesus answering says to them, Have faith in God.
texts.mrk.11.23: Verily I say to you, that whosoever shall say to this mountain, Be thou taken away and cast into the sea, and shall not doubt in his heart, but believe that what he says takes place, whatever he shall say shall come to pass for him.
texts.mrk.11.24: For this reason I say to you, All things whatsoever ye pray for and ask, believe that ye receive it, and it shall come to pass for you.
texts.mrk.11.25: And when ye stand praying, forgive if ye have anything against any one, that your Father also who is in the heavens may forgive you your offences.
texts.mrk.11.26: But if *ye* do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in the heavens forgive your offences.
texts.mrk.11.27: And they come again to Jerusalem. And as he walked about in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders come to him,
texts.mrk.11.28: and they say to him, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority, that thou shouldest do these things?
texts.mrk.11.29: And Jesus answering said to them, *I* also will ask you one thing, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things:
texts.mrk.11.30: The baptism of John, was it of heaven, or of men? answer me.
texts.mrk.11.31: And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we should say, Of heaven, he will say, Why [then] have ye not believed him?
texts.mrk.11.32: but should we say, Of men -- they feared the people; for all held of John that he was truly a prophet.
texts.mrk.11.33: And they answering say to Jesus, We do not know. And Jesus [answering] says to them, Neither do *I* tell you by what authority I do these things.
texts.mrk.12.1: And he began to say to them in parables, A man planted a vineyard, and made a fence round [it] and dug a wine-vat, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and left the country.
texts.mrk.12.2: And he sent a bondman to the husbandmen at the season, that he might receive from the husbandmen of the fruit of the vineyard.
texts.mrk.12.3: But they took him, and beat [him], and sent [him] away empty.
texts.mrk.12.4: And again he sent to them another bondman; and [at] him they [threw stones, and] struck [him] on the head, and sent [him] away with insult.
texts.mrk.12.5: And [again] he sent another, and him they killed; and many others, beating some and killing some.
texts.mrk.12.6: Having yet therefore one beloved son, he sent also him to them the last, saying, They will have respect for my son.
texts.mrk.12.7: But those husbandmen said to one another, This is the heir: come, let us kill him and the inheritance will be ours.
texts.mrk.12.8: And they took him and killed him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard.
texts.mrk.12.9: What therefore shall the lord of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the husbandmen, and will give the vineyard to others.
texts.mrk.12.10: Have ye not even read this scripture, The stone which they that builded rejected, this has become the corner-stone:
texts.mrk.12.11: this is of [the] Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes?
texts.mrk.12.12: And they sought to lay hold of him, and they feared the crowd; for they knew that he had spoken the parable of them. And they left him and went away.
texts.mrk.12.13: And they send to him certain of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, that they might catch him in speaking.
texts.mrk.12.14: And they come and say to him, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and carest not for any one; for thou regardest not men's person, but teachest the way of God with truth: Is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar or not?
texts.mrk.12.15: Should we give, or should we not give? But he knowing their hypocrisy said unto them, Why tempt ye me? Bring me a denarius that I may see [it].
texts.mrk.12.16: And they brought [it]. And he says to them, Whose [is] this image and superscription? And they said to him, Caesar's.
texts.mrk.12.17: And Jesus answering said to them, Pay what is Caesar's to Caesar, and what is God's to God. And they wondered at him.
texts.mrk.12.18: And Sadducees come to him, that say there is no resurrection; and they demanded of him saying,
texts.mrk.12.19: Teacher, Moses wrote to us that if any one's brother die, and leave a wife behind, and leave no children, that his brother shall take his wife, and raise up seed to his brother.
texts.mrk.12.20: There were seven brethren; and the first took a wife, and dying did not leave seed;
texts.mrk.12.21: and the second took her and died, and neither did he leave seed; and the third likewise.
texts.mrk.12.22: And the seven [took her and] did not leave seed. Last of all the woman also died.
texts.mrk.12.23: In the resurrection, when they shall rise again, of which of them shall she be wife, for the seven had her as wife?
texts.mrk.12.24: And Jesus answering said to them, Do not ye therefore err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God?
texts.mrk.12.25: For when they rise from among [the] dead they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as angels [who are] in the heavens.
texts.mrk.12.26: But concerning the dead that they rise, have ye not read in the book of Moses, in [the section of] the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, *I* [am] the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
texts.mrk.12.27: He is not the God of [the] dead, but of [the] living. *Ye* therefore greatly err.
texts.mrk.12.28: And one of the scribes who had come up, and had heard them reasoning together, perceiving that he had answered them well, demanded of him, Which is [the] first commandment of all?
texts.mrk.12.29: And Jesus answered him, [The] first commandment of all [is], Hear, Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord;
texts.mrk.12.30: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thine understanding, and with all thy strength. This is [the] first commandment.
texts.mrk.12.31: And a second like it [is] this: Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is not another commandment greater than these.
texts.mrk.12.32: And the scribe said to him, Right, teacher; thou hast spoken according to [the] truth. For he is one, and there is none other besides him;
texts.mrk.12.33: and to love him with all the heart, and with all the intelligence, and with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love one's neighbour as one's self, is more than all the burnt-offerings and sacrifices.
texts.mrk.12.34: And Jesus, seeing that he had answered intelligently, said to him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And no one dared question him any more.
texts.mrk.12.35: And Jesus answering said [as he was] teaching in the temple, How do the scribes say that the Christ is son of David?
texts.mrk.12.36: [for] David himself said [speaking] in the Holy Spirit, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit on my right hand until I put thine enemies [as] footstool of thy feet.
texts.mrk.12.37: David himself [therefore] calls him Lord, and whence is he his son? And the mass of the people heard him gladly.
texts.mrk.12.38: And he said to them in his doctrine, Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in long robes, and salutations in the marketplaces,
texts.mrk.12.39: and first seats in the synagogues, and first places at suppers;
texts.mrk.12.40: who devour the houses of widows, and as a pretext make long prayers. These shall receive a severer judgment.
texts.mrk.12.41: And Jesus, having sat down opposite the treasury, saw how the crowd was casting money into the treasury; and many rich cast in much.
texts.mrk.12.42: And a poor widow came and cast in two mites, which is a farthing.
texts.mrk.12.43: And having called his disciples to [him] he said to them, Verily I say unto you, This poor widow has cast in more than all who have cast into the treasury:
texts.mrk.12.44: for all have cast in of that which they had in abundance, but she of her destitution has cast in all that she had, the whole of her living.
texts.mrk.13.1: And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples says to him, Teacher, see what stones and what buildings!
texts.mrk.13.2: And Jesus answering said to him, Seest thou these great buildings? not a stone shall be left upon a stone, which shall not be thrown down.
texts.mrk.13.3: And as he sat on the mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,
texts.mrk.13.4: Tell us, when shall these things be, and what is the sign when all these things are going to be fulfilled?
texts.mrk.13.5: And Jesus answering them began to say, Take heed lest any one mislead you.
texts.mrk.13.6: For many shall come in my name, saying, It is *I*, and shall mislead many.
texts.mrk.13.7: But when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be not disturbed, for [this] must happen, but the end is not yet.
texts.mrk.13.8: For nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom; and there shall be earthquakes in [different] places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these things [are the] beginnings of throes.
texts.mrk.13.9: But *ye*, take heed to yourselves, for they shall deliver you up to sanhedrims and to synagogues: ye shall be beaten and brought before rulers and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them;
texts.mrk.13.10: and the gospel must first be preached to all the nations.
texts.mrk.13.11: But when they shall lead you away to deliver you up, be not careful beforehand as to what ye shall say, [nor prepare your discourse]: but whatsoever shall be given you in that hour, that speak; for *ye* are not the speakers, but the Holy Spirit.
texts.mrk.13.12: But brother shall deliver up brother to death, and father child; and children shall rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death.
texts.mrk.13.13: And ye will be hated of all on account of my name; but he that has endured to the end, *he* shall be saved.
texts.mrk.13.14: But when ye shall see the abomination of desolation standing where it should not, (he that reads let him consider [it],) then let those in Judaea flee to the mountains;
texts.mrk.13.15: and him that is upon the housetop not come down into the house, nor enter [into it] to take away anything out of his house;
texts.mrk.13.16: and him that is in the field not return back to take his garment.
texts.mrk.13.17: But woe to those that are with child and to those that give suck in those days!
texts.mrk.13.18: And pray that it may not be in winter time;
texts.mrk.13.19: for those days shall be distress such as there has not been the like since [the] beginning of creation which God created, until now, and never shall be;
texts.mrk.13.20: and if [the] Lord had not cut short those days, no flesh should have been saved; but on account of the elect whom he has chosen, he has cut short those days.
texts.mrk.13.21: And then if any one say to you, Lo, here [is] the Christ, or Lo, there, believe [it] not.
texts.mrk.13.22: For false Christs and false prophets will arise, and give signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the elect.
texts.mrk.13.23: But do *ye* take heed: behold, I have told you all things beforehand.
texts.mrk.13.24: But in those days, after that distress, the sun shall be darkened and the moon shall not give its light;
texts.mrk.13.25: and the stars of heaven shall be falling down, and the powers which are in the heavens shall be shaken;
texts.mrk.13.26: and then shall they see the Son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory;
texts.mrk.13.27: and then shall he send his angels and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from end of earth to end of heaven.
texts.mrk.13.28: But learn the parable from the fig-tree: when its branch already becomes tender and puts forth the leaves, ye know that the summer is near.
texts.mrk.13.29: Thus also *ye*, when ye see these things happening, know that it is near, at the doors.
texts.mrk.13.30: Verily I say unto you, This generation shall in no wise pass away, till all these things take place.
texts.mrk.13.31: The heaven and the earth shall pass away, but my words shall in no wise pass away.
texts.mrk.13.32: But of that day or of that hour no one knows, neither the angels who are in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father.
texts.mrk.13.33: Take heed, watch and pray, for ye do not know when the time is:
texts.mrk.13.34: [it is] as a man gone out of the country, having left his house and given to his bondmen the authority, and to each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper that he should watch.
texts.mrk.13.35: Watch therefore, for ye do not know when the master of the house comes: evening, or midnight, or cock-crow, or morning;
texts.mrk.13.36: lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping.
texts.mrk.13.37: But what I say to you, I say to all, Watch.
texts.mrk.14.1: Now the passover and the [feast of] unleavened bread was after two days. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might seize him by subtlety and kill him.
texts.mrk.14.2: For they said, Not in the feast, lest perhaps there be a tumult of the people.
texts.mrk.14.3: And when he was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, as he lay at table, there came a woman having an alabaster flask of ointment of pure nard, very costly; and having broken the alabaster flask, she poured it out upon his head.
texts.mrk.14.4: And there were some indignant in themselves, and saying, Why has this waste been made of the ointment?
texts.mrk.14.5: for this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor. And they spoke very angrily at her.
texts.mrk.14.6: But Jesus said, Let her alone; why do ye trouble her? she has wrought a good work as to me;
texts.mrk.14.7: for ye have the poor always with you, and whenever ye would ye can do them good; but me ye have not always.
texts.mrk.14.8: What *she* could she has done. She has beforehand anointed my body for the burial.
texts.mrk.14.9: And verily I say unto you, Wheresoever these glad tidings may be preached in the whole world, what this [woman] has done shall be also spoken of for a memorial of her.
texts.mrk.14.10: And Judas Iscariote, one of the twelve, went away to the chief priests that he might deliver him up to them;
texts.mrk.14.11: and they, when they heard it, rejoiced, and promised him to give money. And he sought how he could opportunely deliver him up.
texts.mrk.14.12: And the first day of unleavened bread, when they slew the passover, his disciples say to him, Where wilt thou that we go and prepare, that thou mayest eat the passover?
texts.mrk.14.13: And he sends two of his disciples, and says to them, Go into the city, and a man shall meet you carrying a pitcher of water; follow him.
texts.mrk.14.14: And wheresoever he enters, say to the master of the house, The Teacher says, Where is my guest-chamber where I may eat the passover with my disciples?
texts.mrk.14.15: and *he* will shew you a large upper room furnished ready. There make ready for us.
texts.mrk.14.16: And his disciples went away and came into the city, and found as he had said to them; and they made ready the passover.
texts.mrk.14.17: And when evening was come, he comes with the twelve.
texts.mrk.14.18: And as they lay at table and were eating, Jesus said, Verily I say to you, One of you shall deliver me up; he who is eating with me.
texts.mrk.14.19: And they began to be grieved, and to say to him, one by one, Is it *I*? [and another, Is it *I*?]
texts.mrk.14.20: But he answered and said to them, One of the twelve, he who dips with me in the dish.
texts.mrk.14.21: The Son of man goes indeed as it is written concerning him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is delivered up; [it were] good for that man if he had not been born.
texts.mrk.14.22: And as they were eating, Jesus, having taken bread, when he had blessed, broke [it], and gave [it] to them, and said, Take [this]: this is my body.
texts.mrk.14.23: And having taken [the] cup, when he had given thanks, he gave [it] to them, and they all drank out of it.
texts.mrk.14.24: And he said to them, This is my blood, that of the [new] covenant, that shed for many.
texts.mrk.14.25: Verily I say to you, I will no more drink at all of the fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
texts.mrk.14.26: And having sung a hymn, they went out to the mount of Olives.
texts.mrk.14.27: And Jesus says to them, All ye shall be offended, for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered abroad.
texts.mrk.14.28: But after I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee.
texts.mrk.14.29: But Peter said to him, Even if all should be offended, yet not *I*.
texts.mrk.14.30: And Jesus says to him, Verily I say to thee, that thou to-day, in this night, before [the] cock shall crow twice, thou shalt thrice deny me.
texts.mrk.14.31: But he said [so much] exceedingly the more, If I should have to die with thee, I will in no wise deny thee. And likewise said they all too.
texts.mrk.14.32: And they come to a place of which the name [is] Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples, Sit here while I shall pray.
texts.mrk.14.33: And he takes with him Peter and James and John, and he began to be amazed and oppressed in spirit.
texts.mrk.14.34: And he says to them, My soul is full of grief even unto death; abide here and watch.
texts.mrk.14.35: And, going forward a little, he fell upon the earth; and he prayed that, if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
texts.mrk.14.36: And he said, Abba, Father, all things are possible to thee: take away this cup from me; but not what *I* will, but what *thou* [wilt].
texts.mrk.14.37: And he comes and finds them sleeping. And he says to Peter, Simon, dost thou sleep? Hast thou not been able to watch one hour?
texts.mrk.14.38: Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation. The spirit indeed [is] willing, but the flesh weak.
texts.mrk.14.39: And going away, he prayed again, saying the same thing.
texts.mrk.14.40: And returning, he found them again sleeping, for their eyes were heavy; and they knew not what they should answer him.
texts.mrk.14.41: And he comes the third time and says to them, Sleep on now, and take your rest. It is enough; the hour is come; behold, the Son of man is delivered up into the hands of sinners.
texts.mrk.14.42: Arise, let us go; behold, he that delivers me up has drawn nigh.
texts.mrk.14.43: And immediately, while he was yet speaking, Judas comes up, [being] one of the twelve, and with him a great crowd, with swords and sticks, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
texts.mrk.14.44: Now he that delivered him up had given them a sign between them, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that is he; seize him, and lead [him] away safely.
texts.mrk.14.45: And being come, straightway coming up to him, he says, Rabbi, Rabbi; and he covered him with kisses.
texts.mrk.14.46: And they laid their hands upon him and seized him.
texts.mrk.14.47: But a certain one of those who stood by, having drawn his sword, struck the bondman of the high priest, and took off his ear.
texts.mrk.14.48: And Jesus answering said to them, Are ye come out as against a robber, with swords and sticks to take me?
texts.mrk.14.49: I was daily with you teaching in the temple, and ye did not seize me; but [it is] that the scriptures may be fulfilled.
texts.mrk.14.50: And all left him and fled.
texts.mrk.14.51: And a certain young man followed him with a linen cloth cast about his naked [body]; and [the young men] seize him;
texts.mrk.14.52: but he, leaving the linen cloth behind [him], fled from them naked.
texts.mrk.14.53: And they led away Jesus to the high priest. And there come together to him all the chief priests and the elders and the scribes.
texts.mrk.14.54: And Peter followed him at a distance, till [he was] within the court of the high priest's palace; and he was sitting with the officers and warming himself in the light [of the fire].
texts.mrk.14.55: And the chief priests and the whole sanhedrim sought testimony against Jesus to cause him to be put to death, and did not find [any].
texts.mrk.14.56: For many bore false witness against him, and their testimony did not agree.
texts.mrk.14.57: And certain persons rose up and bore false witness against him, saying,
texts.mrk.14.58: *We* heard him saying, *I* will destroy this temple which is made with hands, and in the course of three days I will build another not made with hands.
texts.mrk.14.59: And neither thus did their testimony agree.
texts.mrk.14.60: And the high priest, rising up before them all, asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? What do these testify against thee?
texts.mrk.14.61: But he was silent, and answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and says to him, *Thou* art the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?
texts.mrk.14.62: And Jesus said, *I* am, and ye shall see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power, and coming with the clouds of heaven.
texts.mrk.14.63: And the high priest, having rent his clothes, says, What need have we any more of witnesses?
texts.mrk.14.64: Ye have heard the blasphemy; what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.
texts.mrk.14.65: And some began to spit upon him, and cover up his face, and buffet him, and say to him, Prophesy; and the officers struck him with the palms of their hands.
texts.mrk.14.66: And Peter being below in the palace-court, there comes one of the maids of the high priest,
texts.mrk.14.67: and seeing Peter warming himself, having looked at him, says, And *thou* wast with the Nazarene, Jesus.
texts.mrk.14.68: But he denied, saying, I know not nor understand what thou sayest. And he went out into the vestibule; and a cock crew.
texts.mrk.14.69: And the maid, seeing him, again began to say to those that stood by, This is [one] of them.
texts.mrk.14.70: And he again denied. And again, after a little, those that stood by said to Peter, Truly thou art [one] of them, for also thou art a Galilean.
texts.mrk.14.71: But he began to curse and to swear, I know not this man of whom ye speak.
texts.mrk.14.72: And the second time a cock crew. And Peter remembered the word that Jesus said to him, Before [the] cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice; and when he thought thereon he wept.
texts.mrk.15.1: And immediately in the morning the chief priests, having taken counsel with the elders and scribes and the whole sanhedrim, bound Jesus and carried [him] away, and delivered [him] up to Pilate.
texts.mrk.15.2: And Pilate asked him, Art *thou* the King of the Jews? And he answered and said to him, *Thou* sayest.
texts.mrk.15.3: And the chief priests accused him urgently.
texts.mrk.15.4: And Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? See of how many things they bear witness against thee.
texts.mrk.15.5: But Jesus still answered nothing, so that Pilate marvelled.
texts.mrk.15.6: But at [the] feast he released to them one prisoner, whomsoever they begged [of him].
texts.mrk.15.7: Now there was the [person] named Barabbas bound with those who had made insurrection with [him], [and] that had committed murder in the insurrection.
texts.mrk.15.8: And the crowd crying out began to beg [that he would do] to them as he had always done.
texts.mrk.15.9: But Pilate answered them saying, Will ye that I release to you the King of the Jews?
texts.mrk.15.10: for he knew that the chief priests had delivered him up through envy.
texts.mrk.15.11: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd that he might rather release Barabbas to them.
texts.mrk.15.12: And Pilate answering said to them again, What will ye then that I do [to him] whom ye call King of the Jews?
texts.mrk.15.13: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
texts.mrk.15.14: And Pilate said to them, What evil then has he done? But they cried out the more urgently, Crucify him.
texts.mrk.15.15: And Pilate, desirous of contenting the crowd, released to them Barabbas, and delivered up Jesus, when he had scourged him, that he might be crucified.
texts.mrk.15.16: And the soldiers led him away into the court which is [called the] praetorium, and they call together the whole band.
texts.mrk.15.17: And they clothe him with purple, and bind round on him a crown of thorns which they had plaited.
texts.mrk.15.18: And they began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!
texts.mrk.15.19: And they struck his head with a reed, and spat on him, and, bending the knee, did him homage.
texts.mrk.15.20: And when they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own clothes on him; and they lead him out that they may crucify him.
texts.mrk.15.21: And they compel to go [with them] a certain passer-by, Simon, a Cyrenian, coming from the field, the father of Alexander and Rufus, that he might carry his cross.
texts.mrk.15.22: And they bring him to the place [called] Golgotha, which, being interpreted, is Place of a skull.
texts.mrk.15.23: And they offered him wine [to drink] medicated with myrrh; but he did not take [it].
texts.mrk.15.24: And having crucified him, they part his clothes amongst [themselves], casting lots on them, what each one should take.
texts.mrk.15.25: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
texts.mrk.15.26: And the superscription of what he was accused of was written up: The King of the Jews.
texts.mrk.15.27: And with him they crucify two robbers, one on his right hand, and one on his left.
texts.mrk.15.28: [And the scripture was fulfilled which says, And he was reckoned with the lawless.]
texts.mrk.15.29: And they that passed by reviled him, shaking their heads, and saying, Aha, thou that destroyest the temple and buildest it in three days,
texts.mrk.15.30: save thyself, and descend from the cross.
texts.mrk.15.31: In like manner the chief priests also, with the scribes, mocking with one another, said, He saved others; himself he cannot save.
texts.mrk.15.32: Let the Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and may believe. And they that were crucified with him reproached him.
texts.mrk.15.33: And when [the] sixth hour was come, there came darkness over the whole land until [the] ninth hour;
texts.mrk.15.34: and at the ninth hour, Jesus cried with a loud voice, [saying], Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
texts.mrk.15.35: And some of those who stood by, when they heard [it], said, Behold, he calls for Elias.
texts.mrk.15.36: And one, running and filling a sponge with vinegar, fixed it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone, let us see if Elias comes to take him down.
texts.mrk.15.37: And Jesus, having uttered a loud cry, expired.
texts.mrk.15.38: And the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom.
texts.mrk.15.39: And the centurion who stood by over against him, when he saw that he had expired having thus cried out, said, Truly this man was Son of God.
texts.mrk.15.40: And there were women also looking on from afar off, among whom were both Mary of Magdala, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
texts.mrk.15.41: who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him and ministered to him; and many others who came up with him to Jerusalem.
texts.mrk.15.42: And when it was already evening, since it was [the] preparation, that is, [the day] before a sabbath,
texts.mrk.15.43: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable councillor, who also himself was awaiting the kingdom of God, coming, emboldened himself and went in to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus.
texts.mrk.15.44: And Pilate wondered if he were already dead; and having called to [him] the centurion, he inquired of him if he had long died.
texts.mrk.15.45: And when he knew from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.
texts.mrk.15.46: And having bought fine linen, [and] having taken him down, he swathed him in the fine linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was cut out of rock, and rolled a stone to the door of the sepulchre.
texts.mrk.15.47: And Mary of Magdala and Mary the [mother] of Joses saw where he was put.
texts.mrk.16.1: And the sabbath being [now] past, Mary of Magdala, and Mary the [mother] of James, and Salome, bought aromatic spices that they might come and embalm him.
texts.mrk.16.2: And very early on the first [day] of the week they come to the sepulchre, the sun having risen.
texts.mrk.16.3: And they said to one another, Who shall roll us away the stone out of the door of the sepulchre?
texts.mrk.16.4: And when they looked, they see that the stone has been rolled [away], for it was very great.
texts.mrk.16.5: And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were amazed and alarmed;
texts.mrk.16.6: but he says to them, Be not alarmed. Ye seek Jesus, the Nazarene, the crucified one. He is risen, he is not here; behold the place where they had put him.
texts.mrk.16.7: But go, tell his disciples and Peter, he goes before you into Galilee; there shall ye see him, as he said to you.
texts.mrk.16.8: And they went out, and fled from the sepulchre. And trembling and excessive amazement possessed them, and they said nothing to any one, for they were afraid.
texts.mrk.16.9: Now when he had risen very early, the first [day] of the week, he appeared first to Mary of Magdala, out of whom he had cast seven demons.
texts.mrk.16.10: *She* went and brought word to those that had been with him, [who were] grieving and weeping.
texts.mrk.16.11: And when these heard that he was alive and had been seen of her, they disbelieved [it].
texts.mrk.16.12: And after these things he was manifested in another form to two of them as they walked, going into the country;
texts.mrk.16.13: and *they* went and brought word to the rest; neither did they believe them.
texts.mrk.16.14: Afterwards as they lay at table he was manifested to the eleven, and reproached [them with] their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
texts.mrk.16.15: And he said to them, Go into all the world, and preach the glad tidings to all the creation.
texts.mrk.16.16: He that believes and is baptised shall be saved, and he that disbelieves shall be condemned.
texts.mrk.16.17: And these signs shall follow those that have believed: in my name they shall cast out demons; they shall speak with new tongues;
texts.mrk.16.18: they shall take up serpents; and if they should drink any deadly thing it shall not injure them; they shall lay hands upon the infirm, and they shall be well.
texts.mrk.16.19: The Lord therefore, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven, and sat at the right hand of God.
texts.mrk.16.20: And they, going forth, preached everywhere, the Lord working with [them], and confirming the word by the signs following upon [it].

texts.mrk.1.1: A beginning of the good news of Jesus Christ, Son of God.
texts.mrk.1.2: As it hath been written in the prophets, `Lo, I send My messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee,' --
texts.mrk.1.3: `A voice of one calling in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, straight make ye his paths,' --
texts.mrk.1.4: John came baptizing in the wilderness, and proclaiming a baptism of reformation -- to remission of sins,
texts.mrk.1.5: and there were going forth to him all the region of Judea, and they of Jerusalem, and they were all baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
texts.mrk.1.6: And John was clothed with camel's hair, and a girdle of skin around his loins, and eating locusts and honey of the field,
texts.mrk.1.7: and he proclaimed, saying, `He doth come -- who is mightier than I -- after me, of whom I am not worthy -- having stooped down -- to loose the latchet of his sandals;
texts.mrk.1.8: I indeed did baptize you with water, but he shall baptize you with the Holy Spirit.'
texts.mrk.1.9: And it came to pass in those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John at the Jordan;
texts.mrk.1.10: and immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens dividing, and the Spirit as a dove coming down upon him;
texts.mrk.1.11: and a voice came out of the heavens, `Thou art My Son -- the Beloved, in whom I did delight.'
texts.mrk.1.12: And immediately doth the Spirit put him forth to the wilderness,
texts.mrk.1.13: and he was there in the wilderness forty days, being tempted by the Adversary, and he was with the beasts, and the messengers were ministering to him.
texts.mrk.1.14: And after the delivering up of John, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of the reign of God,
texts.mrk.1.15: and saying -- `Fulfilled hath been the time, and the reign of God hath come nigh, reform ye, and believe in the good news.'
texts.mrk.1.16: And, walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon, and Andrew his brother, casting a drag into the sea, for they were fishers,
texts.mrk.1.17: and Jesus said to them, `Come ye after me, and I shall make you to become fishers of men;'
texts.mrk.1.18: and immediately, having left their nets, they followed him.
texts.mrk.1.19: And having gone on thence a little, he saw James of Zebedee, and John his brother, and they were in the boat refitting the nets,
texts.mrk.1.20: and immediately he called them, and, having left their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired servants, they went away after him.
texts.mrk.1.21: And they go on to Capernaum, and immediately, on the sabbaths, having gone into the synagogue, he was teaching,
texts.mrk.1.22: and they were astonished at his teaching, for he was teaching them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
texts.mrk.1.23: And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
texts.mrk.1.24: saying, `Away! what -- to us and to thee, Jesus the Nazarene? thou didst come to destroy us; I have known thee who thou art -- the Holy One of God.'
texts.mrk.1.25: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, `Be silenced, and come forth out of him,'
texts.mrk.1.26: and the unclean spirit having torn him, and having cried with a great voice, came forth out of him,
texts.mrk.1.27: and they were all amazed, so as to reason among themselves, saying, `What is this? what new teaching [is] this? that with authority also the unclean spirits he commandeth, and they obey him!'
texts.mrk.1.28: And the fame of him went forth immediately to all the region, round about, of Galilee.
texts.mrk.1.29: And immediately, having come forth out of the synagogue, they went to the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John,
texts.mrk.1.30: and the mother-in-law of Simon was lying fevered, and immediately they tell him about her,
texts.mrk.1.31: and having come near, he raised her up, having laid hold of her hand, and the fever left her immediately, and she was ministering to them.
texts.mrk.1.32: And evening having come, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all who were ill, and who were demoniacs,
texts.mrk.1.33: and the whole city was gathered together near the door,
texts.mrk.1.34: and he healed many who were ill of manifold diseases, and many demons he cast forth, and was not suffering the demons to speak, because they knew him.
texts.mrk.1.35: And very early, it being yet night, having risen, he went forth, and went away to a desert place, and was there praying;
texts.mrk.1.36: and Simon and those with him went in quest of him,
texts.mrk.1.37: and having found him, they say to him, -- `All do seek thee;'
texts.mrk.1.38: and he saith to them, `We may go to the next towns, that there also I may preach, for for this I came forth.'
texts.mrk.1.39: And he was preaching in their synagogues, in all Galilee, and is casting out the demons,
texts.mrk.1.40: and there doth come to him a leper, calling on him, and kneeling to him, and saying to him -- `If thou mayest will, thou art able to cleanse me.'
texts.mrk.1.41: And Jesus having been moved with compassion, having stretched forth the hand, touched him, and saith to him, `I will; be thou cleansed;'
texts.mrk.1.42: and he having spoken, immediately the leprosy went away from him, and he was cleansed.
texts.mrk.1.43: And having sternly charged him, immediately he put him forth,
texts.mrk.1.44: and saith to him, `See thou mayest say nothing to any one, but go away, thyself shew to the priest, and bring near for thy cleansing the things Moses directed, for a testimony to them.'
texts.mrk.1.45: And he, having gone forth, began to proclaim much, and to spread abroad the thing, so that no more he was able openly to enter into the city, but he was without in desert places, and they were coming unto him from every quarter.
texts.mrk.2.1: And again he entered into Capernaum, after [some] days, and it was heard that he is in the house,
texts.mrk.2.2: and immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even at the door, and he was speaking to them the word.
texts.mrk.2.3: And they come unto him, bringing a paralytic, borne by four,
texts.mrk.2.4: and not being able to come near to him because of the multitude, they uncovered the roof where he was, and, having broken [it] up, they let down the couch on which the paralytic was lying,
texts.mrk.2.5: and Jesus having seen their faith, saith to the paralytic, `Child, thy sins have been forgiven thee.'
texts.mrk.2.6: And there were certain of the scribes there sitting, and reasoning in their hearts,
texts.mrk.2.7: `Why doth this one thus speak evil words? who is able to forgive sins except one -- God?'
texts.mrk.2.8: And immediately Jesus, having known in his spirit that they thus reason in themselves, said to them, `Why these things reason ye in your hearts?
texts.mrk.2.9: which is easier, to say to the paralytic, The sins have been forgiven to thee? or to say, Rise, and take up thy couch, and walk?
texts.mrk.2.10: `And, that ye may know that the Son of Man hath authority on the earth to forgive sins -- (he saith to the paralytic) --
texts.mrk.2.11: I say to thee, Rise, and take up thy couch, and go away to thy house;'
texts.mrk.2.12: and he rose immediately, and having taken up the couch, he went forth before all, so that all were astonished, and do glorify God, saying -- `Never thus did we see.'
texts.mrk.2.13: And he went forth again by the sea, and all the multitude was coming unto him, and he was teaching them,
texts.mrk.2.14: and passing by, he saw Levi of Alpheus sitting at the tax-office, and saith to him, `Be following me,' and he, having risen, did follow him.
texts.mrk.2.15: And it came to pass, in his reclining (at meat) in his house, that many tax-gatherers and sinners were reclining (at meat) with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
texts.mrk.2.16: And the scribes and the Pharisees, having seen him eating with the tax-gatherers and sinners, said to his disciples, `Why -- that with the tax-gatherers and sinners he doth eat and drink?'
texts.mrk.2.17: And Jesus, having heard, saith to them, `They who are strong have no need of a physician, but they who are ill; I came not to call righteous men, but sinners to reformation.'
texts.mrk.2.18: And the disciples of John and those of the Pharisees were fasting, and they come and say to him, `Wherefore do the disciples of John and those of the Pharisees fast, and thy disciples do not fast?'
texts.mrk.2.19: And Jesus said to them, `Are the sons of the bride-chamber able, while the bridegroom is with them, to fast? so long time as they have the bridegroom with them they are not able to fast;
texts.mrk.2.20: but days shall come when the bridegroom may be taken from them, and then they shall fast -- in those days.
texts.mrk.2.21: `And no one a patch of undressed cloth doth sew on an old garment, and if not -- the new filling it up doth take from the old and the rent doth become worse;
texts.mrk.2.22: and no one doth put new wine into old skins, and if not -- the new wine doth burst the skins, and the wine is poured out, and the skins will be destroyed; but new wine into new skins is to be put.'
texts.mrk.2.23: And it came to pass -- he is going along on the sabbaths through the corn-fields -- and his disciples began to make a way, plucking the ears,
texts.mrk.2.24: and the Pharisees said to him, `Lo, why do they on the sabbaths that which is not lawful?'
texts.mrk.2.25: And he said to them, `Did ye never read what David did, when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him?
texts.mrk.2.26: how he went into the house of God, (at `Abiathar the chief priest,') and the loaves of the presentation did eat, which it is not lawful to eat, except to the priests, and he gave also to those who were with him?'
texts.mrk.2.27: And he said to them, `The sabbath for man was made, not man for the sabbath,
texts.mrk.2.28: so that the son of man is lord also of the sabbath.'
texts.mrk.3.1: And he entered again into the synagogue, and there was there a man having the hand withered,
texts.mrk.3.2: and they were watching him, whether on the sabbaths he will heal him, that they might accuse him.
texts.mrk.3.3: And he saith to the man having the hand withered, `Rise up in the midst.'
texts.mrk.3.4: And he saith to them, `Is it lawful on the sabbaths to do good, or to do evil? life to save, or to kill?' but they were silent.
texts.mrk.3.5: And having looked round upon them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their heart, he saith to the man, `Stretch forth thy hand;' and he stretched forth, and his hand was restored whole as the other;
texts.mrk.3.6: and the Pharisees having gone forth, immediately, with the Herodians, were taking counsel against him how they might destroy him.
texts.mrk.3.7: And Jesus withdrew with his disciples unto the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judea,
texts.mrk.3.8: and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon -- a great multitude -- having heard how great things he was doing, came unto him.
texts.mrk.3.9: And he said to his disciples that a little boat may wait on him, because of the multitude, that they may not press upon him,
texts.mrk.3.10: for he did heal many, so that they threw themselves on him, in order to touch him -- as many as had plagues;
texts.mrk.3.11: and the unclean spirits, when they were seeing him, were falling down before him, and were crying, saying -- `Thou art the Son of God;'
texts.mrk.3.12: and many times he was charging them that they might not make him manifest.
texts.mrk.3.13: And he goeth up to the mountain, and doth call near whom he willed, and they went away to him;
texts.mrk.3.14: and he appointed twelve, that they may be with him, and that he may send them forth to preach,
texts.mrk.3.15: and to have power to heal the sicknesses, and to cast out the demons.
texts.mrk.3.16: And he put on Simon the name Peter;
texts.mrk.3.17: and James of Zebedee, and John the brother of James, and he put on them names -- Boanerges, that is, `Sons of thunder;'
texts.mrk.3.18: and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Cananite,
texts.mrk.3.19: and Judas Iscariot, who did also deliver him up; and they come into a house.
texts.mrk.3.20: And come together again doth a multitude, so that they are not able even to eat bread;
texts.mrk.3.21: and his friends having heard, went forth to lay hold on him, for they said that he was beside himself,
texts.mrk.3.22: and the scribes who [are] from Jerusalem having come down, said -- `He hath Beelzeboul,' and -- `By the ruler of the demons he doth cast out the demons.'
texts.mrk.3.23: And, having called them near, in similes he said to them, `How is the Adversary able to cast out the Adversary?
texts.mrk.3.24: and if a kingdom against itself be divided, that kingdom cannot be made to stand;
texts.mrk.3.25: and if a house against itself be divided, that house cannot be made to stand;
texts.mrk.3.26: and if the Adversary did rise against himself, and hath been divided, he cannot be made to stand, but hath an end.
texts.mrk.3.27: `No one is able the vessels of the strong man -- having entered into his house -- to spoil, if first he may not bind the strong man, and then his house he will spoil.
texts.mrk.3.28: `Verily I say to you, that all the sins shall be forgiven to the sons of men, and evil speakings with which they might speak evil,
texts.mrk.3.29: but whoever may speak evil in regard to the Holy Spirit hath not forgiveness -- to the age, but is in danger of age-during judgment;'
texts.mrk.3.30: because they said, `He hath an unclean spirit.'
texts.mrk.3.31: Then come do his brethren and mother, and standing without, they sent unto him, calling him,
texts.mrk.3.32: and a multitude was sitting about him, and they said to him, `Lo, thy mother and thy brethren without do seek thee.'
texts.mrk.3.33: And he answered them, saying, `Who is my mother, or my brethren?'
texts.mrk.3.34: And having looked round in a circle to those sitting about him, he saith, `Lo, my mother and my brethren!
texts.mrk.3.35: for whoever may do the will of God, he is my brother, and my sister, and mother.'
texts.mrk.4.1: And again he began to teach by the sea, and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he, having gone into the boat, sat in the sea, and all the multitude was near the sea, on the land,
texts.mrk.4.2: and he taught them many things in similes, and he said to them in his teaching:
texts.mrk.4.3: `Hearken, lo, the sower went forth to sow;
texts.mrk.4.4: and it came to pass, in the sowing, some fell by the way, and the fowls of the heaven did come and devour it;
texts.mrk.4.5: and other fell upon the rocky ground, where it had not much earth, and immediately it sprang forth, because of not having depth of earth,
texts.mrk.4.6: and the sun having risen, it was scorched, and because of not having root it did wither;
texts.mrk.4.7: and other fell toward the thorns, and the thorns did come up, and choke it, and fruit it gave not;
texts.mrk.4.8: and other fell to the good ground, and was giving fruit, coming up and increasing, and it bare, one thirty-fold, and one sixty, and one an hundred.'
texts.mrk.4.9: And he said to them, `He who is having ears to hear -- let him hear.'
texts.mrk.4.10: And when he was alone, those about him, with the twelve, did ask him of the simile,
texts.mrk.4.11: and he said to them, `To you it hath been given to know the secret of the reign of God, but to those who are without, in similes are all the things done;
texts.mrk.4.12: that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they may turn, and the sins may be forgiven them.'
texts.mrk.4.13: And he saith to them, `Have ye not known this simile? and how shall ye know all the similes?
texts.mrk.4.14: He who is sowing doth sow the word;
texts.mrk.4.15: and these are they by the way where the word is sown: and whenever they may hear, immediately cometh the Adversary, and he taketh away the word that hath been sown in their hearts.
texts.mrk.4.16: `And these are they, in like manner, who on the rocky ground are sown: who, whenever they may hear the word, immediately with joy do receive it,
texts.mrk.4.17: and have not root in themselves, but are temporary; afterward tribulation or persecution having come because of the word, immediately they are stumbled.
texts.mrk.4.18: `And these are they who toward the thorns are sown: these are they who are hearing the word,
texts.mrk.4.19: and the anxieties of this age, and the deceitfulness of the riches, and the desires concerning the other things, entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.
texts.mrk.4.20: `And these are they who on the good ground have been sown: who do hear the word, and receive, and do bear fruit, one thirty-fold, and one sixty, and one an hundred.'
texts.mrk.4.21: And he said to them, `Doth the lamp come that under the measure it may be put, or under the couch -- not that it may be put on the lamp-stand?
texts.mrk.4.22: for there is not anything hid that may not be manifested, nor was anything kept hid but that it may come to light.
texts.mrk.4.23: If any hath ears to hear -- let him hear.'
texts.mrk.4.24: And he said to them, `Take heed what ye hear; in what measure ye measure, it shall be measured to you; and to you who hear it shall be added;
texts.mrk.4.25: for whoever may have, there shall be given to him, and whoever hath not, also that which he hath shall be taken from him.'
texts.mrk.4.26: And he said, `Thus is the reign of God: as if a man may cast the seed on the earth,
texts.mrk.4.27: and may sleep, and may rise night and day, and the seed spring up and grow, he hath not known how;
texts.mrk.4.28: for of itself doth the earth bear fruit, first a blade, afterwards an ear, afterwards full corn in the ear;
texts.mrk.4.29: and whenever the fruit may yield itself, immediately he doth send forth the sickle, because the harvest hath come.'
texts.mrk.4.30: And he said, `To what may we liken the reign of God, or in what simile may we compare it?
texts.mrk.4.31: As a grain of mustard, which, whenever it may be sown on the earth, is less than any of the seeds that are on the earth;
texts.mrk.4.32: and whenever it may be sown, it cometh up, and doth become greater than any of the herbs, and doth make great branches, so that under its shade the fowls of the heaven are able to rest.'
texts.mrk.4.33: And with many such similes he was speaking to them the word, as they were able to hear,
texts.mrk.4.34: and without a simile he was not speaking to them, and by themselves, to his disciples he was expounding all.
texts.mrk.4.35: And he saith to them on that day, evening having come, `We may pass over to the other side;'
texts.mrk.4.36: and having let away the multitude, they take him up as he was in the boat, and other little boats also were with him.
texts.mrk.4.37: And there cometh a great storm of wind, and the waves were beating on the boat, so that it is now being filled,
texts.mrk.4.38: and he himself was upon the stern, upon the pillow sleeping, and they wake him up, and say to him, `Teacher, art thou not caring that we perish?'
texts.mrk.4.39: And having waked up, he rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, `Peace, be stilled;' and the wind did lull, and there was a great calm:
texts.mrk.4.40: and he said to them, `Why are ye so fearful? how have ye not faith?'
texts.mrk.4.41: and they feared a great fear, and said one to another, `Who, then, is this, that even the wind and the sea do obey him?'
texts.mrk.5.1: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the region of the Gadarenes,
texts.mrk.5.2: and he having come forth out of the boat, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
texts.mrk.5.3: who had his dwelling in the tombs, and not even with chains was any one able to bind him,
texts.mrk.5.4: because that he many times with fetters and chains had been bound, and pulled in pieces by him had been the chains, and the fetters broken in pieces, and none was able to tame him,
texts.mrk.5.5: and always, night and day, in the mountains, and in the tombs he was, crying and cutting himself with stones.
texts.mrk.5.6: And, having seen Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed before him,
texts.mrk.5.7: and having called with a loud voice, he said, `What -- to me and to thee, Jesus, Son of God the Most High? I adjure thee by God, mayest thou not afflict me!'
texts.mrk.5.8: (for he said to him, `Come forth, spirit unclean, out of the man,')
texts.mrk.5.9: and he was questioning him, `What [is] thy name?' and he answered, saying, `Legion [is] my name, because we are many;'
texts.mrk.5.10: and he was calling on him much, that he may not send them out of the region.
texts.mrk.5.11: And there was there, near the mountains, a great herd of swine feeding,
texts.mrk.5.12: and all the demons did call upon him, saying, `Send us to the swine, that into them we may enter;'
texts.mrk.5.13: and immediately Jesus gave them leave, and having come forth, the unclean spirits did enter into the swine, and the herd did rush down the steep place to the sea -- and they were about two thousand -- and they were choked in the sea.
texts.mrk.5.14: And those feeding the swine did flee, and told in the city, and in the fields, and they came forth to see what it is that hath been done;
texts.mrk.5.15: and they come unto Jesus, and see the demoniac, sitting, and clothed, and right-minded -- him having had the legion -- and they were afraid;
texts.mrk.5.16: and those having seen [it], declared to them how it had come to pass to the demoniac, and about the swine;
texts.mrk.5.17: and they began to call upon him to go away from their borders.
texts.mrk.5.18: And he having gone into the boat, the demoniac was calling on him that he may be with him,
texts.mrk.5.19: and Jesus did not suffer him, but saith to him, `Go away to thy house, unto thine own [friends], and tell them how great things the Lord did to thee, and dealt kindly with thee;
texts.mrk.5.20: and he went away, and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how great things Jesus did to him, and all were wondering.
texts.mrk.5.21: And Jesus having passed over in the boat again to the other side, there was gathered a great multitude to him, and he was near the sea,
texts.mrk.5.22: and lo, there doth come one of the chiefs of the synagogue, by name Jairus, and having seen him, he doth fall at his feet,
texts.mrk.5.23: and he was calling upon him much, saying -- `My little daughter is at the last extremity -- that having come, thou mayest lay on her [thy] hands, so that she may be saved, and she shall live;'
texts.mrk.5.24: and he went away with him. And there was following him a great multitude, and they were thronging him,
texts.mrk.5.25: and a certain woman, having an issue of blood twelve years,
texts.mrk.5.26: and many things having suffered under many physicians, and having spent all that she had, and having profited nothing, but rather having come to the worse,
texts.mrk.5.27: having heard about Jesus, having come in the multitude behind, she touched his garment,
texts.mrk.5.28: for she said -- `If even his garments I may touch, I shall be saved;'
texts.mrk.5.29: and immediately was the fountain of her blood dried up, and she knew in the body that she hath been healed of the plague.
texts.mrk.5.30: And immediately Jesus having known in himself that out of him power had gone forth, having turned about in the multitude, said, `Who did touch my garments?'
texts.mrk.5.31: and his disciples said to him, `Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and thou sayest, `Who did touch me!'
texts.mrk.5.32: And he was looking round to see her who did this,
texts.mrk.5.33: and the woman, having been afraid, and trembling, knowing what was done on her, came, and fell down before him, and told him all the truth,
texts.mrk.5.34: and he said to her, `Daughter, thy faith hath saved thee; go away in peace, and be whole from thy plague.'
texts.mrk.5.35: As he is yet speaking, there come from the chief of the synagogue's [house, certain], saying -- `Thy daughter did die, why still dost thou harass the Teacher?'
texts.mrk.5.36: And Jesus immediately, having heard the word that is spoken, saith to the chief of the synagogue, `Be not afraid, only believe.'
texts.mrk.5.37: And he did not suffer any one to follow with him, except Peter, and James, and John the brother of James;
texts.mrk.5.38: and he cometh to the house of the chief of the synagogue, and seeth a tumult, much weeping and wailing;
texts.mrk.5.39: and having gone in he saith to them, `Why do ye make a tumult, and weep? the child did not die, but doth sleep;
texts.mrk.5.40: and they were laughing at him. And he, having put all forth, doth take the father of the child, and the mother, and those with him, and goeth in where the child is lying,
texts.mrk.5.41: and, having taken the hand of the child, he saith to her, `Talitha cumi;' which is, being interpreted, `Damsel (I say to thee), arise.'
texts.mrk.5.42: And immediately the damsel arose, and was walking, for she was twelve years [old]; and they were amazed with a great amazement,
texts.mrk.5.43: and he charged them much, that no one may know this thing, and he said that there be given to her to eat.
texts.mrk.6.1: And he went forth thence, and came to his own country, and his disciples do follow him,
texts.mrk.6.2: and sabbath having come, he began in the synagogue to teach, and many hearing were astonished, saying, `Whence hath this one these things? and what the wisdom that was given to him, that also such mighty works through his hands are done?
texts.mrk.6.3: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, and Joses, and Judas, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us?' -- and they were being stumbled at him.
texts.mrk.6.4: And Jesus said to them -- `A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his kindred, and in his own house;'
texts.mrk.6.5: and he was not able there any mighty work to do, except on a few infirm people having put hands he did heal [them];
texts.mrk.6.6: and he wondered because of their unbelief. And he was going round the villages, in a circle, teaching,
texts.mrk.6.7: and he doth call near the twelve, and he began to send them forth two by two, and he was giving them power over the unclean spirits,
texts.mrk.6.8: and he commanded them that they may take nothing for the way, except a staff only -- no scrip, no bread, no brass in the girdle,
texts.mrk.6.9: but having been shod with sandals, and ye may not put on two coats.
texts.mrk.6.10: And he said to them, `Whenever ye may enter into a house, there remain till ye may depart thence,
texts.mrk.6.11: and as many as may not receive you, nor hear you, going out thence, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony to them; verily I say to you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom or Gomorrah in a day of judgment than for that city.'
texts.mrk.6.12: And having gone forth they were preaching that [men] might reform,
texts.mrk.6.13: and many demons they were casting out, and they were anointing with oil many infirm, and they were healing [them].
texts.mrk.6.14: And the king Herod heard, (for his name became public,) and he said -- `John the Baptist out of the dead was raised, and because of this the mighty powers are working in him.'
texts.mrk.6.15: Others said -- `It is Elijah,' and others said -- `It is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.'
texts.mrk.6.16: And Herod having heard, said -- `He whom I did behead -- John -- this is he; he was raised out of the dead.'
texts.mrk.6.17: For Herod himself, having sent forth, did lay hold on John, and bound him in the prison, because of Herodias the wife of Philip his brother, because he married her,
texts.mrk.6.18: for John said to Herod -- `It is not lawful to thee to have the wife of thy brother;'
texts.mrk.6.19: and Herodias was having a quarrel with him, and was willing to kill him, and was not able,
texts.mrk.6.20: for Herod was fearing John, knowing him a man righteous and holy, and was keeping watch over him, and having heard him, was doing many things, and hearing him gladly.
texts.mrk.6.21: And a seasonable day having come, when Herod on his birthday was making a supper to his great men, and to the chiefs of thousands, and to the first men of Galilee,
texts.mrk.6.22: and the daughter of that Herodias having come in, and having danced, and having pleased Herod and those reclining (at meat) with him, the king said to the damsel, `Ask of me whatever thou wilt, and I will give to thee,'
texts.mrk.6.23: and he sware to her -- `Whatever thou mayest ask me, I will give to thee -- unto the half of my kingdom.'
texts.mrk.6.24: And she, having gone forth, said to her mother, `What shall I ask for myself?' and she said, `The head of John the Baptist;'
texts.mrk.6.25: and having come in immediately with haste unto the king, she asked, saying, `I will that thou mayest give me presently, upon a plate, the head of John the Baptist.'
texts.mrk.6.26: And the king -- made very sorrowful -- because of the oaths and of those reclining (at meat) with him, would not put her away,
texts.mrk.6.27: and immediately the king having sent a guardsman, did command his head to be brought,
texts.mrk.6.28: and he having gone, beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head upon a plate, and did give it to the damsel, and the damsel did give it to her mother;
texts.mrk.6.29: and having heard, his disciples came and took up his corpse, and laid it in the tomb.
texts.mrk.6.30: And the apostles are gathered together unto Jesus, and they told him all, and how many things they did, and how many things they taught,
texts.mrk.6.31: and he said to them, `Come ye yourselves apart to a desert place, and rest a little,' for those coming and those going were many, and not even to eat had they opportunity,
texts.mrk.6.32: and they went away to a desert place, in the boat, by themselves.
